#4583. Hyundai Has a Clever Way to Add Power to a Two-Way Tailgate

A little transmission would let one drive motor raise and lower the whole tailgate or swing one section sideways.

Multifunction and split tailgates are definitely a thing now, and there’s probably no going back. Many truckmakers offer some sort of door-within-a-door or built-in-step arrangement that adds utility to what was previously just a hinged wall that kept stuff in the bed. A new Hyundai/Kia concept could take that to the next level by applying power to a two-way tailgate.

A recently published U.S. patent application covering a previously disclosed design builds on previous filings that describe a split tailgate that opens two ways: the conventional way, swinging the whole unit down with hinge action at the bottom, or sideways opening, with a vertical hinge allowing a portion of the tailgate to swing out, providing belly-up-to-the-bed access. That much we've seen before.

See all results for used Hyundai for sale near 97058

The distinguishing feature is that this split tailgate can open and close in either direction, and do so with power from a single drive motor. All two-way tailgates currently offered by Ford, Honda, and Ram require manual operation for side-opening, and only Ford’s offers powered raising and lowering. Not only does the Hyundai/Kia idea remove that unnecessary application of work, but it does so with clever simplicity.

Think of the mechanism as a little transmission that sends one drive motor’s power to either of two outputs. One operates the bottom hinge to raise or lower the entire tailgate. The other operates a spindle that pushes or pulls a lever to swing one section sideways. A second motor operates the clutch mechanism that selects between them. So there are two motors, but only one does the work of moving the tailgate.

Sure, you could figure out a way to package two drive motors into such a tailgate or its surroundings, but that’s unnecessary complexity and likely more weight. The latest patent describes control logic that should avoid any expensive crashes. Before beginning either opening sequence, the controller checks that both tailgate latches are engaged and the vehicle is stopped. It then selects the appropriate drive path, releases the corresponding latch, and powers the gate open.

One notable design difference seen in the application’s drawings is that the vertical hinge lives at the seam between the tailgate’s two sections, not on the truck bed as in Honda’s and Ram’s production implementations, and the side-opening portion latches to the truck’s box. Ford also uses a mid-tailgate vertical hinge, but its panel within a panel is surrounded by more tailgate on either side.

See all results for used Hyundai for sale near 97058

If something like this were to make production, it would most likely turn up on the mid-size body-on-frame pickup Hyundai has promised. We’ve also seen a patent for a hardtop for the related SUV that would allow for one-person roof assembly. There’s nothing that says both innovations couldn’t end up on both of the new off-roaders, but of course there's no guarantee of either.

He can parallel-park a school bus and once drove a Lincoln Town Car 63 mph in reverse. After taking a break from journalism to work on autonomous vehicles, he’s back writing for this and other automotive publications. #4582. New Jersey is putting 10 MW of community solar on warehouse roofs

Warehouse roofs are prime real estate for solar, and Faropoint is putting more of that underused space to work in New Jersey. The industrial property owner has started construction on the first of 16 community solar projects totaling more than 10 megawatts (MW).

First up is a 1.6 MW rooftop array at 19-05 Nevins Road in Fair Lawn. Another 15 projects, totaling about 8.5 MW, have been accepted into New Jersey’s Community Solar Energy Program, and nine are already cleared to start construction.

That’s more solar going onto buildings that are already there, with participating households set to get savings on their electricity bills.

Large warehouse roofs offer something solar developers need: lots of flat space. Putting panels up there gives the same building the job of generating electricity without taking up additional land.

Faropoint specializes in industrial properties used for local deliveries and distribution. “Utilizing previously unused portions of our buildings allows us to support the communities where we invest,” said Brian Nave, Faropoint’s vice president of asset management and renewable energy.

Faropoint and its independent solar adviser, SolarKal, expect the 16 projects to generate around 12.7 million kilowatt-hours (kWh) of electricity annually once they’re operating. They estimate the portfolio will avoid about 8,500 metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions a year.

Faropoint says at least half of each project’s capacity will be reserved for low- and moderate-income households. New Jersey’s program requires a minimum of 51%.

Excellent. There are so many warehouses around here, it always baffled me that they weren't all covered with solar panels. Next we gotta get to work on all the parking lots.

Faropoint and SolarKal have not yet announced completion dates, subscription prices, or enrollment details for their New Jersey warehouse roof community solar portfolio.

#4581. Segway launches new electric motorcycle that’s so safe it has seatbelts

Segway came to EICMA this year with a surprisingly broad lineup of new electric motorcycles, ranging from high-performance concepts to off-road machines. But perhaps the most interesting of the bunch is also the one that looks the least like a conventional motorcycle or scooter.

Meet the Segway X Cruiser, an electric two-wheeler that takes motorcycle safety so seriously that it has a roll cage and seatbelts.

Or at least, those are among the configurations Segway is showing as it develops the new machine for production.

The X Cruiser is Segway’s attempt to bring more automotive-style protection to a single-track vehicle, essentially asking how much of a car’s safety envelope can be wrapped around a motorcycle without adding another pair of wheels.

From the looks of things, the answer is quite a lot.

Segway says the X Cruiser’s design was informed by automotive crash scenarios, with cage and semi-cage structures, four-direction collision protection, staged energy absorption, and seatbelt restraints intended to improve rider protection. It also gets active safety features including standard blind spot detection and lane change warning.

The company showed several ways that basic idea can be configured, ranging from a more conventional partially enclosed scooter-like setup to versions with significantly more structure surrounding the rider. One of the most striking configurations uses a heavily bolstered race-car-style seat and seatbelt along with protective framing around the rider, while another adds a roof for even more enclosure.

It’s a fascinating approach because motorcycles have traditionally relied largely on the rider wearing the protection. Helmets, jackets, gloves, boots and sometimes airbag vests form the safety system, while the motorcycle itself generally offers little physical protection during a crash.

The X Cruiser effectively flips part of that equation by building some of the protective structure into the vehicle itself.

There’s an important caveat here, though. Segway specifically notes that its descriptions refer to the vehicle’s current design and equipment and do not mean it has completed automotive-style crash certification. Final equipment and certification will depend on individual markets, so it sounds like the company is holding short of making any major certification claims. Still though, it’s easy to see how having what is effectively a racing seat and roll cage surrounding the rider could seriously contribute to better protection in a crash. Just remember to keep your hands and feet within the vehicle at all times.

And unlike plenty of wild EICMA showpieces, this one isn’t merely destined to live under convention-center spotlights. Segway says the X Cruiser has a confirmed mass-production plan, with launches planned for China and Europe between 2027 and 2028. There’s no US availability announcement yet.

Underneath all that protective hardware is a fairly serious electric touring platform. Segway is using its CTB (cell-to-body) battery integration to help improve structural rigidity and battery packaging, with the company targeting nearly 200 km (124 miles) of range.

European versions are expected to feature 4.5 kW Type 2 AC charging, while the Chinese version will offer optional higher-power DC fast charging. The bike rolls on 15-inch front and 14-inch rear wheels wearing Michelin City Grip tires, and riders get a 10.25-inch TFT display along with an optional 55-liter electrically operated top box.

Interestingly, the X Cruiser also incorporates certain two-wheeler intellectual property and know-how licensed from BMW Group, though Segway stresses that it is responsible for the vehicle’s development, integration, validation, production and certification.

The X Cruiser may be the weirdest – and thus perhaps the most interesting – of Segway’s EICMA debuts, but it was far from alone.

The company also unveiled the Segway Orca Concept, a futuristic high-performance electric maxi-scooter concept built around an 800V electrical architecture and a nearly 20 kWh battery.

Segway is targeting up to 300 km (186 miles) of range, a 0-100 km/h (0-62 mph) time of 4.5 seconds, and the ability to add 200 km (124 miles) of range in 20 minutes. The concept also features front and rear multi-link suspension, electronically controlled multi-mode damping and a battery-integrated CTB chassis. Those figures are engineering targets rather than promised production specifications, and Segway currently describes the Orca strictly as a concept.

Its a BMW C1 reborn as electric! They were a bit of a cult thing, but underpowered for the weight. Never made it to the USA.

The biggest benefit is not really safety, its comfort.

Then there’s Segway’s expanding X Series, which moves the focus away from urban riding and toward dirt. The lineup includes the Xaber X1000 and Xaber 350, along with different Xaber 300 variants for the US and European markets. Segway is also partnering with Michelin for its Dakar Rally Factory Team, using the brutal rally environment as a real-world development and validation platform for electric off-road motorcycles.

Taken together, it’s quite the showing from a company whose name many people still associate primarily with those funny two-wheeled self-balancing machines from the early 2000s.

Segway has already expanded heavily into electric scooters, e-bikes, go-karts and powersports vehicles. Now it seems increasingly serious about becoming an electric motorcycle company as well.

And if motorcycles with roll cages, roofs and seatbelts are part of that future, things could get pretty interesting… pretty quickly!

#4580. Farah: Why a Fender Bender in My Porsche Taycan Cost $35,000

A minor accident in my late-model EV nearly totaled it, and the battery pack was partly to blame.

I love cars, but I also know cars are bad for the environment, whether they are powered by gas, electric, or diesel. New cars, in particular, take energy and raw materials to build, and often cost more to run and maintain. For me, that upfront environmental impact is all the more reason to keep older, efficient cars on the road even in the face of rising repair costs. But there must be a balance in the quest for efficiency.

If you do care about the planet, the most efficient choice in the U.S. right now is to buy a used, well-maintained EV. No one built a brand new car for you, and the carbon footprint from assembling it is now spread across multiple owners. The longer you drive it, the cleaner it is (versus a combustion car).

For nearly two years, I have been driving around L.A. in what was, as of December of 2024, the cheapest used Porsche Taycan Cross Turismo in the United States. I love EVs for driving around cities just as much as I love a high-compression, light-flywheel, manual gearbox, mid-engined monster for a canyon run: each is fit for its purpose. I did not buy a used EV to make some kind of political or environmental statement—I saw personal value and a fun public experiment. After all, a Taycan depreciates rapidly from new, and not because it’s a badly made car.

What originally stickered for $139,000 was mine for $64,800 plus tax with only 26,000 miles. Over the approximately 12,000 miles since, it has been a superb car: comfortable, fast, dynamic, and overwhelmingly reliable, albeit with a few software hiccups and two genuine mechanical repairs, all sorted under the Porsche Certified pre-owned unlimited-mile warranty. Although a Taycan is still a semi-exotic Porsche to many, the four-seat electric wagon is my family’s most “normal” car.

Which is why I let a friend borrow it for a trip to the lake with his wife. My friend isn’t a car enthusiast, but he had no history of accidents, shenanigans, or other red flags in the 30 years I’ve known him. The perfect person to trust with a loan. And so I never would have predicted the phone call I received over that weekend: He’d been in an accident with my car.

Fortunately, no one was hurt. Also fortunately (for our relationship), the accident wasn’t his fault, as insisted by him, bolstered by a police report, and cosigned by my insurance adjuster. In fact, he was stopped at a red light and rear-end/sideswiped by a young woman who, as it turns out, had a long history of accidents in her short driving career.

And while I was upset to get the phone call, my rage subsided quickly when I saw the accident site photo. This didn’t look like a big deal at all. The rear bumper was scraped, and perhaps the parking sensor was damaged. The painted-over fender needed replacing, as did the HRE 522M wheel. I figured maybe $3000-4000 for the body work, another $4000 for the wheel, a couple of weeks in the shop, and that would be that.

It would be 73 days, and it would cost my insurance company over $35,000 before I got my car back. Hypothetically, if the car was not insured under an agreed-value classic car collector’s policy, it would likely have been outright totaled, despite being easily repairable.

It turns out the impact on the damaged wheel, plus the force of the car being shoved several feet while the brakes were applied, damaged the air suspension. It wasn’t just damaged on the corner that was hit. Both the gas strut and control arm assembly were cracked on the opposite corner as well, even without a direct impact! When the air suspension lost pressure, the air supply unit, control module, and a bunch of other four-figure components went down with it. Once the suspension needs to be disassembled to that degree, Porsche isn’t going to reassemble it with old hardware, so the invoice includes thousands in bolts, bushings, collar nuts, washers, carriers, and so on.

And because it's an EV, performing this work requires removing the high-voltage battery pack: 24 hours at $340 an hour. If you aren’t used to paying for mechanical work, this is a huge rate, even for Porsches, even in Los Angeles.

So while the cosmetic bodywork amounted to little more than $5000 or $6000, the mechanical and electrical repairs escalated like Bitcoin in 2020, eventually landing in the mid-twenties. Factor in a new wheel from HRE, three flatbed transports, and assorted random billables, and that’s how the total made it to $35,000.

The air suspension took second place on the bill; the Achilles' heel for late-model luxury car service, gas or electric alike. It was almost $20,000. This and all other repairs would have been similar to a gas-powered Panamera or Cayenne. But if you're predisposed to hate EVs, here's another piece of ammunition towards that view. Nearly $8000 of this bill, over 20% of it, went to battery pack labor. (The pack itself was, and is, totally fine).

As these once-pricey EVs get cheaper, the cost of repairs raises the value required to avoid getting totaled. This is a shame. Otherwise working, good-condition cars with most of their carbon footprint already amortized might be scrapped. Yes, battery packs and cells can be recycled, but it’s not done at a large enough scale yet. More importantly, the best thing we can do for the environment is keep already-built EV’s on the road for as long as possible. Fortunately, battery packs are lasting longer in cars than originally expected (ironically part of the reason for the slow build of the battery recycling ecosystem).

To their credit, both South Bay Certified Collision Center in Torrance, CA, and McKenna Porsche did an excellent job repairing my car. This is not a story about getting ripped off, and I’m not arguing that any other shop could do it cheaper. The fact that my Taycan got a completely refreshed air suspension means it drives perhaps even better than it did before. And because I have agreed value insurance and the accident wasn’t my fault, none of the enormous stack of dollars it took to fix my car came out of my pocket. I could have chosen to total the car, but I chose to fix it. Such is the benefit of that type of policy. And I intend to keep driving this car because I very much like it.

If we are going to have more EV’s, which we should, because they are good for many things, then we need to ensure that these cars survive minor collisions. That could mean changing what the word “totaled” means for an EV on the insurance side. It could also mean training up enough technicians so that a battery pack removal doesn’t command a higher hourly rate than what I pay for Lamborghini Countach restoration. It should also mean that car companies, perhaps German ones, should design battery packs so that they’re more easily removed or that other major components can be replaced around them.

In either case, we can’t have EVs meeting a premature demise. There’s nothing more wasteful than a car that could be working, but without working math to justify fixing it.

Matt Farah is a lifelong car enthusiast who began his automotive career at dealerships, rental agencies, and detail shops before discovering the power of YouTube in 2006, with his channel The Smoking Tire. #4579. Acura Kicks Off Sales of More Than 3000 Official Reproduction Parts for the 1st-Gen NSX

Acura’s NSX heritage parts program moves from announcement to U.S. sales, giving owners fresh support for their aging supercars.

Buying or owning an older supercar is one thing. Keeping it on the road is another issue, and that's only complicated further when it comes to finding replacement parts. Acura is now making that aspect of ownership about as easy as it could possibly be for first-gen NSX owners: this week, the brand is officially kicking off sales of more than 3000 reproduction parts through its Honda Heritage Parts program.

The new welcome development for NSX owners comes through Acura dealerships nationwide and through Honda's DreamShop. The reality here is that, although great cars like the NSX have exceptional enthusiast support, factory-backed parts re-creation is hard to match. It's one thing to hope you'll find a part across used listings and another to know it's available at a local dealer.

If all this sounds familiar, it's for good reason. As Road & Track reported in March, the company has been intending to bring reproduction parts to American dealers for a minute now. This latest development moves the story along to actual sales. That said, there are two very clear sides to this business: “Genuine Honda Reproduction Parts” use the same materials and production methods as the original components; “Honda Compatible Parts” are redeveloped replacements for original pieces that the company no longer sells.

See all results for used Honda for sale near 90011

That differentiation allows the brand to build what it feels makes sense and lean on suppliers elsewhere. Originally, Acura said it would cover the powertrain, interior, exterior, electrical, and chassis components. That's a wide swath to be sure—but for now, owners will still need to check availability to be sure that the individual piece they need is available.

That said, all of this signals just how key the NSX is to Acura and Honda. Supporting a supercar decades after production helps owners keep and maintain the car in question. In addition, it gives prospective buyers a touch more confidence about picking one up. In other words, it could boost the second-hand market and the overarching value of the nameplate itself. That won't make an NSX (or any other supercar) cheap or easy to maintain, but it eases some of the frustration.

BYD launched the new Seal 07 in China, where it starts at around $23,000. It’s about the size of a Toyota Camry, but brings a surprising amount of tech and premium features for the money.

After introducing the updated first-generation Seal 07 in March, BYD launched the second-gen model on Thursday.

The second-generation Seal 07, which BYD calls the “new choice for a class-leading luxury experience,” is available in battery electric (EV) and plug-in hybrid (PHEV) powertrains.

BYD offers five variants, including two PHEVs and three EVs, starting at 139,900 yuan (about $21,000) for the plug-in hybrid and 149,900 yuan (around $22,500) for the fully electric version.

The new Seal 07 EV uses a 76.7 kWh second-generation BYD Blade LFP battery, providing a CLTC range of up to 481 miles (775 km).

It comes standard with a single rear-mounted electric motor producing up to 328 hp (245 kW) and 269 lb-ft (365 Nm) of torque, which BYD says enables it to accelerate from 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 km/h) in 5.5 seconds.

All plug-in hybrid variants use BYD’s latest DM-i system, which features a 1.5L turbocharged engine with 154 hp (115 kW) and a 214 hp (160 kW) front electric motor.

The new Seal 07 PHEV has a smaller 37 kWh battery that provides up to 205 miles (330 km) of pure electric CLTC range. That’s a considerable jump from the 143 miles (230 km) of electric range the previous generation offered.

Thanks to BYD’s latest Blade Battery 2.0 and Flash Charging technology, the vehicle’s battery can recharge from 10% to 70% in just 5 minutes. To go from 10% to 97%, it takes just nine minutes.

Both versions are 5,080 mm long, 1,960 mm wide, and 1,495 mm tall, with a 2,960 mm wheelbase, which is slightly bigger than the Toyota Camry.

Inside, the new Seal 07 adopts BYD’s latest cabin design, including a 15.6″ floating center infotainment screen, a 10.25″ instrument cluster, and two rear passenger entertainment screens.

BYD added several premium extras, including a built-in 6.8L smart refrigerator, zero gravity seats, and driver headrest audio. It also offers the most rear passenger space and the largest frunk (160L) in its class, according to BYD.

The Seal 07 debuts BYD’s Smart Ecosystem 2.0, including “Diva,” a smartwatch that can interact with the vehicle and let drivers manage functions remotely.

Higher-priced models offer BYD’s God’s Eye B intelligent driving system, with a roof-mounted LiDAR available as an option. The setup provides safety and convenience features such as Navigation on Autopilot in the city and on highways, plus full-scenario intelligent parking.

BYD is offering a limited-time “Super trade-in price” promo, starting at 145,900 yuan ($22,000) for the new Seal 07 EV and 135,900 yuan ($20,500) for the PHEV version.

The 0-Series EV line may never reach production, but the new logo and design language those cars inspired seem to be on the way soon.

When Honda abandoned its plans to release a series of 0-Series-branded electric vehicles earlier this year, it also effectively abandoned the first cars that would have been released in the company’s bold new design language. That certainly does not mean the new look of Honda is being tabled forever, though. Both Honda of Australia and Honda of Japan posted a teaser for a model called the Avancier on Friday, revealing a first look at an SUV expected to be targeted primarily at those markets. Notably, the model appears to bear a passing resemblance to both the scrapped 0-Series SUV and the May concept. “Honda Hybrid” badging also suggests that the Avancier will be one of the company’s first cars to use the brand’s next-generation gas-electric powertrain.

The Avancier badge has previously been used on a turn-of-the-millennium station wagon for Japan, as well as a Chinese-built crossover offered in that market. This new model seems to be a crossover targeted at other markets, something that could be equivalent to the American CR-V or Passport. Details of the final model, including specifics of the Honda Hybrid powertrain, may prove irrelevant to American buyers, but the styling and the concepts behind the hybrid system could preview what to expect when Honda unveils a fast-tracked new CR-V for the United States in the near future.

#4575. Tesla wants its sworn Cybercab answers to NHTSA kept entirely secret

Tesla has answered NHTSA’s Special Order demanding it prove, under oath, that the Cybercab meets federal safety standards. The response landed on the October 30 deadline, and Tesla asked the agency to keep all of it confidential.

The only part of the filing the public can read is a 30-page guide for firefighters. Everything about how a car with no steering wheel, pedals, or mirrors was certified as compliant is blacked out.

We reported in September that NHTSA had ordered Tesla to show its work on the Cybercab’s certification. The order came one week after the company started charging for Cybercab rides in Austin on September 3 and put 21 questions to the company, with civil penalties of up to $139 million for an incomplete answer and criminal exposure for a false one.

Tesla first tried to buy time. On September 18, it asked for eight more weeks, until November 20, citing “the voluminous nature of the request” and the work of searching its records and writing “thorough narrative formats in response to each question.” NHTSA gave it 30 days instead. The new deadline was October 30, and Tesla met it.

Three Tesla documents now sit in the AQ26002 docket, and two of them are empty.

The first is Tesla’s response letter, dated October 30 and addressed from 1 Tesla Road in Austin. It is one page long. The only text is: “The entirety of this file is confidential business information.”

The second is a placeholder for Tesla’s answer to Request 8, which asked the company to explain, standard by standard, how it determined the Cybercab complies: which subpart it certified to, and whether it ran physical tests, simulations, or engineering analyses. Per NHTSA’s note, the responsive documents carry a confidentiality request “for the entirety of each document.”

The third is the only substantive document: Tesla’s Cybercab First Responder Interaction Plan, version 1.2, dated September 3. It’s a real document with useful information in it. It’s also something Tesla has had on its website since July, aimed at police and fire crews, not regulators.

So the public gets a tow-truck manual, and the certification argument stays sealed.

The Special Order wasn’t a fishing expedition. It named the rules the Cybercab doesn’t obviously meet, and it seeks to understand how Tesla believes it can get around it.

FMVSS 135 says “the service brakes shall be activated by means of a foot control.” NHTSA has stated in public that a manufacturer of a vehicle with no foot brake can’t certify to it, then asked Tesla how it did. FMVSS 108 requires a turn-signal control that cancels itself when the steering wheel turns. FMVSS 111 requires mirrors. And the agency wanted to know whether Tesla certified the car with temporary driver controls bolted in and then removed them, which would run into the Safety Act’s “make inoperative” prohibition.

It also asked how the Cybercab is legal without a Part 555 exemption, the route Amazon’s Zoox took for its own steering-wheel-less robotaxi in July. Zoox applied, made its case, and got an exemption capped at 2,500 vehicles a year. Tesla self-certified and started charging for rides.

Every one of those answers is now under a confidentiality claim.

The first-responder plan was written for a different audience, but it brushes against several of NHTSA’s questions.

It says the Cybercab is “not typically equipped with a steering wheel or acceleration and brake pedals.” The word “typically” is doing work there. The same document notes that a Cybercab with a steering wheel and pedals “is typically an engineering or test vehicle, and operates at SAE Level 2 autonomy,” and includes instructions for driving one. That’s relevant to Requests 5 through 7, which asked whether the subject vehicles can be driven with temporarily attached controls.

It describes an operational design domain covering “all public roadways, such as freeways, highways, city streets, and rural roads,” at all hours, in light and moderate rain, fog, and snow. That is a far wider envelope than the Austin geofence the cars run in today, and it references an “Arizona Areas of Operation Appendix.” Request 1 asked for the ODD and Request 2 for scaling plans.

And it confirms that first responders can be granted access to on-board touchscreen controls to move the car, after showing a badge to the B-pillar camera (that’s interesting). Request 20 asked whether the touchscreen can move the vehicle and under what restrictions.

Nothing in it touches brakes, mirrors, telltales, or the certification itself.

Confidentiality requests go to NHTSA’s Chief Counsel under Part 512. The agency decides whether Tesla’s claim holds, and it can order a public version released if it doesn’t. NHTSA hasn’t said anything about the request, and it hasn’t found the Cybercab noncompliant with any standard.

This is familiar. In June 2025, Tesla asked NHTSA to hide its answers about the original Robotaxi launch in Austin, a service running on supervised FSD while FSD was under investigation. Those answers never surfaced.

NHTSA’s opening resume for the audit put the affected population at about 1,000 vehicles. The Cybercab is still carrying passengers in Austin while the agency reads a filing nobody else can.

I don't see how the answers can have confidential business secrets. It is about meeting public safety standards, not asking for schematics, technical details or designs. It is about clear public safety requirement and how the vehicle qualify as meeting it.

The so called keyword from Tesla's self certification is "applicable". Tesla may argue that many of those requirements aren't applicable in their test vehicle. But I would like to see the justifications on that.

Tesla’s position in September was that the Cybercab complies with every applicable federal standard, including the one that requires a brake pedal. If that’s true, the argument for it is the most interesting document in the autonomous vehicle industry right now, and Tesla just asked the government to make sure nobody reads it.

We get why a company redacts test data and supplier details. But the legal theory for how a car with no foot brake meets a foot-brake rule doesn’t sound like a trade secret to me. Zoox’s exemption petition is public. Waymo’s safety framework is public. Tesla’s case for why it didn’t need to ask is sealed, cover letter included.

NHTSA now has to decide whether “the entirety of this file” is really confidential business information. If it says no, we’ll finally see how Tesla certified this car. If it says yes, about 1,000 Cybercabs keep driving on a certification the public isn’t allowed to check.

With decades of experience in gaming and a full tour as a Gaming Journalist, Michael is ready to step up to the plate. From AAA to the smallest passion projects, his motto is that every piece of ar

Many studios have been in rough patches recently, either due to internal struggles amid the modern challenges of development or due to layoffs or closures mandated by larger owners. It's easy to write off every issue in the modern industry as someone else’s fault, but that’s not realistic; every part of the industry is struggling, inside and out.

The upcoming God of War spin-off has been delayed to May 20th, dodging the busy February release window.

Arkane Lyon is one studio that's been in hot water for a long while, struggling to find a buyer before Microsoft closes its doors. Following hopeful news as more buyers step up, a French union with ties to Arkane staff has accused Microsoft of attempting to sabotage the development of the studio’s current project, Blade, by barring hires for over a year.

The development of Marvel’s Blade has been absolutely hectic, between internal shifts in the game’s vision and an early announcement that put heat on Arkane far before they were ready. Now, STJV, the French union representing certain members of Arkane Lyon’s staff, has made a major accusation, claiming the game is coming along fine, despite Microsoft’s interference.

According to STJV in a direct quotation, “Today, as work on Blade is going fine, and the level of quality of the game to be expected is on [par] with what Arkane has accustomed its players, workers have to face the harsh reality: our studio might get closed because, and only because, Microsoft decided to, even if that means sabotaging the game it funded.”

This all still has yet to be confirmed, as no direct response from Microsoft has been released, despite the accusations levied by STJV. Alongside the biting remarks, the union has dropped a series of demands, including a say in who buys Arkane, and a larger payout for the staff if no buyer steps forward.

It's easy to write off every issue in the modern industry as someone else’s fault, but that’s not realistic, every part of the industry is struggling, inside and out.

Despite all of this swinging out, Arkane is still eager to release Blade, staying optimistic that the title will release in the following years if Arkane is allowed to keep their doors open. STJV keeps the argument practical, framing the studio’s progress as a financial incentive for both parties. “Even this closure itself is done against any financial logic, as closing Arkane today would probably be more expensive than finishing the game,” says STJV.

Arkane’s aim to finish the game despite their wild situation is comforting to see, and gives me real hope at the quality of their Blade title, as long as it manages to release. The whispers of big studios like Ubisoft’s interest make it clear more than just Arkane want to see the title released, and as the months continue to tick by with the company still open, those whispers just get louder.

Arkane is a studio that would feel like a serious loss for the larger gaming industry if they closed their doors, even after stumbles like Redfall. Dropping into the mainstream scene with hits like Dishonored and Prey, Arkane Lyon is infamous for worlds that feel so lived-in, even after devastation has raked across them.

They truly do feel like the perfect team to work on Blade, as their mastery of immersive sims and wild powers leaves massive room for the exact type of action Blade is perfect for. It really does feel like every production surrounding Blade is hexed, if the canceled films and Arkane’s own pains are anything to look at.

I’m very eager to hear a response from Microsoft, as STJV has levied some major accusations that could really disrupt how third parties and internal studios interact with them. At present, we only have STJV’s word to go off of, so take these accusations with a grain of salt until more comes out.

#4573. Hyundai Recalls 38K Vehicles Over Faulty Airbags and Seatbelts

The recall covers certain Veloster N and Kona Electric models and stems from a software error.

Hyundai issued a recall over a concerning safety issue that could affect as many as 37,901 vehicles, documents filed with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) show. According to the recall paperwork, the recall covers some 2019–2022 Veloster N and 2019–2023 Kona Electric vehicles, whose airbags and seatbelt pretensioners may not deploy in a crash.

The recall population is split between 8843 Velosters and 29,058 Konas. According to the recall documents, the issue with the airbags and seatbelt pretensioners originates from a software error. Each of the affected cars comes equipped with an Airbag Control Unit, or ACU, that detects crash signals and instructs the airbags and seatbelt pretensioners to deploy. The NHTSA documents show that the ACU’s software may be corrupted when the system reboots while the ACU is writing data to its internal memory. At a minimum, there is a warning to notify drivers of the issue. If the ACU’s data is corrupted, the airbag malfunction indicator light will illuminate on the dashboard.

See all results for used 2022 Hyundai Veloster N for sale near 14094

The recall comes after more than a year of testing and attempts to recreate the issue by both Hyundai and the ACU’s supplier, following an increase in airbag warranty light claims that was identified in August 2024. As of October 2026, Hyundai was aware of 331 reported incidents alleging the recall complaint, though, thankfully, the company was not aware of any crashes, fires, or injuries.

Owners of affected vehicles will be instructed to bring their car to a Hyundai dealer, where technicians will update the ACU software. The update will be performed for free, and Hyundai will reimburse owners for out-of-pocket expenses incurred to get the fix before the recall was filed. Letters notifying both Hyundai dealers and affected owners of the recall will be mailed on January 1, 2027.

#4572. Hyundai is recalling nearly 30,000 Kona Electric vehicles due to an airbag software defect

Hyundai issued a recall affecting nearly 30,000 Kona Electric vehicles due to a software error that could cause the airbag to fail to deploy in a crash.

In a letter sent to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration on November 4, Hyundai said it was recalling certain 2019 to 2023 Kona Electric and 2019 to 2022 Veloster N vehicles.

The recall impacts 37,901 vehicles in total, including 29,058 Kona Electric and 8,843 Veloster N models.

According to documents submitted to the NHTSA, the issue stems from a software error with the airbag control unit (ACU) that can cause the airbag malfunction indicator light (MIL) to come on and the airbag system to deactivate under certain driving conditions.

The data may become corrupted during a system reboot or power interruption while the system is writing to the ACU’s memory. When this happens, the airbag MIL will illuminate to warn drivers.

As of October 22, 2026, Hyundai is aware of 331 alleged incidents related to the issue. However, none have resulted in a crash, fire, or injury.

Owners can take their vehicle to the closest dealer, where it will update the ACU software, free of charge.

Hyundai expects to mail out owner notification letters on January 1, 2027. In the meantime, owners can contact Hyundai’s customer service at 1-855-371-9460 with any questions or concerns. Hyundai’s recall number is 311.

You can also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 or visit the NHTSA.gov website for more information. The NHTSA campaign number is 26V728.

Official EPA numbers are not yet available, but we estimate the GT55 and GT63 models will deliver between 85 and 92 MPGe combined. MPGe stands for miles per gallon of gas equivalent, an EPA metric that estimates PHEV and EV vehicle fuel efficiency.

First Row: The interior of the GT features racy touches such as carbon-fiber trim and AMG-specific displays, but incorporates the kind of upscale materials you would expect from a high-zoot Mercedes. You sit low in the sports seats, and the steering wheel features paddle shifters.

Second Row: The rear seat is sculpted, and the standard setup only seats two passengers. A three-passenger bench seat is optional.

Cargo Capacity: The GT’s trunk accomodates 15 cubic feet, and there’s a small front trunk under the hood. When we get the chance, we’ll see how many carry-on suitcases we can fit inside.

The GT has a 10.2-inch digital gauge cluster and a 14.0-inch central touchscreen that’s angled towards the driver. It runs Mercedes’ MBUX software and has a highly customizable display. There’s also a standard passenger’s display screen. Mercedes offers subscriptions to many connectivity features, and a head-up display is optional.

The GT comes with standard driver-assistance technology including forward-collision warning, blind-spot monitoring and automated emergency braking, as well as lane-departure warning and lane-keeping assist. More advanced tech is available as part of a subscription.

For information about the GT's crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites.

The GT has the same warranty coverage as other Mercedes EVs, which is nothing out of the ordinary. Other luxury automakers, such as BMW and Jaguar, provide some amount of complimentary maintenance, whereas Mercedes does not.

#4569. Sonic Pico Park Review: A Great Party Favor

Sonic the Hedgehog becomes friends with the cute little cats of Pico Park, inviting all of us into a co-op puzzle-platformer that's sure to make you laugh one way or another.

This year marks the big 3-5 for Sega’s patented Mario killer, Sonic the Hedgehog. It’s been an eventful time for all kinds of fans. Of course, it’s hard to celebrate this momentous occasion with the all but ignored elephant in the room that is the mainline game Sonic Team has all but officially unveiled that’s still in development. But we aren’t going without a game for the anniversary, at least!

Enter Sonic Pico Park. Like the title implies, it’s a return to the chaotic co-op world of Pico Park with a new hedgehog-shaped coat of paint. Ever since it was announced in time for the blue blur’s birthday, Sonic Pico Park has been teasing the mechanics and playable characters slowly leading up to the game’s November launch. It’s been a nice little treat between Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds DLC, monthly comics, and a stream of other goodies throughout the year. But there’s a question that I’m sure a lot of us want to ask.

Sonic the Hedgehog is turning 35 this year, and if you're looking for games to celebrate the occasion, there are plenty of options for you.

Is Sonic Pico Park a good game for this milestone? Is it as good and as cute as it’s been advertised? Is it more Pico than Sonic? Luckily for you, I’m here to answer these questions and more. A short answer to keep things quick: Yes, and no. And if that makes you happy, let’s get into deeper details so you know what you’re getting into before dragging your friends into playing with you.

I’ll be honest and say that it’s hard for me to not fall victim to Sonic Pico Park’s charms. I’ve always adored sprite art. Seeing some of my favorite characters of all time as these miniaturized, big-headed versions, dancing around and reflecting their personalities in these quick animations is just too good to resist. But there’s more to Sonic Pico Park than that.

Like the original Pico Park, Sonic Pico Park is a co-op game where teamwork is key to win. It can be played with at least two players, but you can navigate this game with eight people max if you really want these short and sweet levels to be complete ragers in two different senses of the word. I got to team up with two other writers to play this game. The fun of Sonic Pico Park definitely grows with the number of players involved.

The puzzling co-op of Pico Park fits like a glove with Sonic’s trademark speed. If you thought the original Pico Park may have been too slow, this game picks up the pace with ease without making anything too uncontrollable or without giving you and your friends time to think things through. There are fewer twists to the levels that gave Pico Park what fame it has here, though, likely to keep things less frustrating for younger players and their families. Saboteurs who purposefully ignore instructions for a laugh will still have their ways, though.

Plenty of Pico Park gimmicks, like buttons, numbered platforms and blocks, are scattered throughout the level with springs, loop-de-loops, and rings from Sonic. There are more Sonic mechanics to play with throughout the whole game than Pico staples, and there are plenty of surprises for the average Sonic fan to spot. It’s because of these features that Sonic Pico Park really sticks out as a Sonic game, and one that certainly rises to the 35th anniversary occasion. But like most parties, it will end and become a good memory in time.

One important factor Sonic fans should understand before jumping into Sonic Pico Park is that the games that came before it aren’t particularly long. Pico Park itself only takes about three hours, and I managed to play everything the game offered in about four and a half hours according to my playtime stats. Thankfully this balances out with Sonic Pico Park’s asking price, which I think is fair for a cute little romp with friends. Especially since all it takes is for one of those friends to choose violence and a level that would take five minutes has now taken fifteen because everyone’s too busy laughing and screaming to get back on track. You know. Typical co-op game stuff.

As a Sonic game, Sonic Pico Park is a great snack for the hungry, but won’t be enough for the ravenous.

Sonic fans will still have fun seeing the unexpected twists to what Pico Park is known for. If you remove the Sonic flavoring, you can still find a fun platformer underneath, but the personality of each of the playable Sonic characters really completes the experience. It gives it a sense of style that blends both games together to create something unique that fans will love. It might also serve as the perfect gateway for any Sonic-obsessed friends to finally pull you into this series. Play at your own risk.

Without going into too many details, Sonic Pico Park sticks the landing as an anniversary game. There are a lot of surprises to find in this game as you go along, but it comes at the price of the game’s identity at times that might rub a few players the wrong way. There’s an element to Pico Park that remains in these moments, bringing in a new challenge of figuring out how to tackle the old with the new. But that might not be enough to save these moments from feeling like jingling keys to a fan worn out on the last decade or so of nostalgic references.

Still, that’s only a more cynical look at things. Among the game’s levels and modes, I feel like there are far more interesting twists on Sonic mechanics with Pico Park-style platforming and puzzle-solving than anything else. As a Sonic game, Sonic Pico Park is a great snack for the hungry, but won’t be enough for the ravenous. But it might satiate them a little if their friends bring the laughs and some good nibbles to go with it.

Any newcomers to Sonic don’t have to worry much. Sonic Pico Park doesn’t overstay its welcome. There are a few modes to play on the side, and you can always drag more friends into the chaos and not backseat them, but otherwise, it’s hard to see groups of friends coming back to Sonic Pico Park after clearing everything the first time. And sometimes, it’s okay if a party doesn’t last forever. What’s important is the chaos and fun you have with the people you share it with that will stay with you long after those few hours are up.

Sonic Pico Park is a step up for the iconic puzzle-platformer. It adds a sense of style and quick-thinking that only Sonic could bring to Pico Park while giving an element of chaos not entirely new to Sonic, but elevated through the humor of Pico Park. The dedication and love to the Sonic series can be felt in everything it squeezes into its short run time, as well as how every single character’s personality is made far bigger than the sprites used to portray them. It might not be the game fans expected out of this year, but it’s certainly what they need and deserve. Sonic Pico Park, like the games that came before it, will bring plenty of laughs and good memories to players long after this anniversary is over.

#4568. This Startup Is Turning Used E-Bike Batteries Into Affordable Energy Storage

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Millions of e-bike and e-scooter batteries are thrown away every year, even though they might still have life in them. Now, a German startup is trying to reduce battery waste by integrating used batteries from e-mobility vehicles into energy storage systems.

EDENenergy, which has just three part-time staff members in addition to its three founders, has shipped its first commercial product, a 70-kilowatt-hour battery system that uses no fewer than 112 second-life e-scooter batteries.

All modules were thoroughly tested, and the results were better than expected. The company’s founders, who used to be researchers at the Fraunhofer Institute for Solar Energy Systems ISE, said that they expected the old batteries to have roughly 80% life left in them, but the tests revealed that most retained about 90% of their original capacity.

After being abused in their previous life, the e-scooter batteries will have a much easier future in the startup’s energy storage systems, where vibrations and large temperature fluctuations are non-existent. What’s more, the long-term energy capacity of the system can be easily kept at 70 kWh by simply replacing modules that become unusable down the line.

The startup said it remotely monitors each module, and when it’s time for a replacement, it can be done without powering down the whole system. That’s a big plus, especially for energy-sensitive scenarios where cutting the power would result in massive losses.

The keen-eyed among you might have noticed that there’s a solar inverter on one side of the battery box. That’s because EDENenergy’s first product was designed for companies that have solar panels but can’t store solar energy yet. “In mid-October, we delivered the first storage system to a customer, which was an important milestone for our young company,” said Florian Bierwirth, one of the founders. “With this storage size, we initially aim to target medium-sized companies in the region that have a photovoltaic system but do not yet have a storage solution.”

For its next step, the startup wants to come up with a way of using different batteries from different manufacturers. “To do this, the connector interfaces, battery management system, and communication protocols must be adapted for each new battery. There’s a particularly wide range of options when it comes to e-bikes,” said Bierwirth. Currently, the small company relies on large suppliers that can send in large numbers of the same battery type.

A larger-capacity battery system of up to 300 kWh is also in the works, putting roughly 500 second-life e-scooter modules to good use instead of sending them to the landfill. The batteries will eventually give up, but when that happens, they’ll be sent to a recycling facility where they’ll be dismantled, and their contents will be reused, if possible.

#4567. EVs Made Up Nearly A Third Of UK Sales As Europe's Electric Boom Continues

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

While EV sales are growing slowly in the U.S., despite the loss of federal tax incentives, they're exploding in the UK. According to UK's car industry lobby New Automotive, 49,155 new fully battery-electric vehicles (BEV) were sold in October. That's not only a massive 54% increase over last October, but it's 32% of the UK's new car market share, or almost a third.

That 32% market share also gave EVs the largest market share of any one fuel type, more than gas, diesel, or hybrids. "Almost one in three new cars sold in October was fully electric, more than any other fuel type, and electric car sales are up by more than half on last year," said Ben Nelmes, CEO at New AutoMotive. "Drivers are voting with their wallets. Every one of those new electric cars means a household spending less on running costs, and a country less exposed to the oil price shock."

There's more EV variety in the UK than there is in America. The UK has access to EVs from brands like Renault, Peugeot, Fiat, Volkswagen, Skoda, and even Chinese EVs like BYD and Jaecoo. Last month, Kia, BMW, Volkswagen, and BYD led the country's electric market. Tesla slumped after a big September.

Year-to-date, though, Tesla is number one, with 9.53% market share. That's up 25.4% from last year, too. Kia took second place, with 6.9% market share, and BYD came in third, with 6.8%. What's surprising is that no European EV brands were in the top three, despite being in their home continent. I'd sell a non-essential organ for a Renault 5 E-Tech, so I'm surprised to see cars like that not taking top spots in the UK.

It isn't just new EVs, either. The UK is also seeing a jump in used EVs, just like we are here. According to EV Powered, data shows that more and more UK customers are shopping for used EVs.

The run up in oil costs is driving record EV sales across Europe. BEVs took 37% share of the car market in Germany, the country's road traffic agency said, with over 94,000 vehicles sold. That's a nearly 80% increase year over year.

#4565. China Has An Iron Grip On EV Batteries. Here's America’s Plan To Break It

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

The U.S. Department of Energy last week released a new three-step plan to localize the supply chain of batteries and reduce America’s reliance on China. The plan may not even mention electric vehicles, but the EV market could be among its biggest beneficiaries if successfully executed.

Citing data from research firm BloombergNEF, the DOE said demand for batteries would increase four fold between 2025 and 2035, from 179 gigawatt-hours to 707 GWh. The demand is expected to skyrocket across sectors including transportation, the power grid, AI data centers, consumer electronics, and drones.

While the report acknowledged that America’s battery cell and pack manufacturing had improved over the past few years, the core supply chain was still heavily reliant on imports. That means things like raw material mining and the production of a battery’s subcomponents such as anodes, cathodes, electrolytes, and separators were still largely happening overseas, mostly in China.

To fix this, DOE said a new three-step plan was necessary, and the following are its objectives:

In part one of this plan, the focus would be to invest in the battery supply chain. “DOE is prioritizing investments to shift from a discontinuous, import-reliant supply chain to an integrated domestic production system through the upstream (mining), midstream (refining and engineered materials), and downstream (cells, packs, and end products),” the DOE said. It added that it would focus on targeted investments in companies that specialize in extraction, recycling, refining, and equipment manufacturing.

Part two outlines developing and commercializing next-generation batteries that are right for their specific applications. “These batteries should be more affordable, longer lasting, higher performing, and less reliant on critical minerals in select market segments,” the DOE said. So think solid-state cells or more advanced versions of current lithium-ion technology. And the final part of the plan is to get them past the “valley of death,” meaning converting discoveries made in the lab into actual products people can buy.

To be clear, the Biden administration had shared similar objectives back in 2021 in far more detail with a focus on clean energy, social justice, and equitable jobs. The Trump administration’s blueprint is much thinner and instead leans on national security, the grid, humanoid robots, and the enormous power demands of AI data centers. It doesn't explicitly mention EVs, but instead says next-gen batteries would also help in the transportation sector.

It's also worth remembering that America's battery industry was surging long before that. After Trump swept to power in 2024, battery manufacturing in the U.S. took a severe hit. According to clean energy think tank E2, the U.S. canceled, closed or downsized battery projects worth $42 billion between 2022 and 2026, costing the nation over 85,000 jobs. Across the broader clean energy sector, the sum increases to $137 billion, costing over 240,000 jobs, according to the same report.

The new blueprint is still a step in the right direction, even if it is more of a continued effort. It also reflects how much the battery landscape has changed since the start of the decade. EV sales have been up and down, while demand for stationary energy storage has surged, driven by utility upgrades and AI data centers. The revised strategy accounts for that shift, and automakers could still benefit over the long term for their EV plans.

If you like the TX but are seeking more grunt, consider the TX Hybrid, which we review separately. On the road, the TX350 feels less peppy than its hybrid sibling, but its quiet and comfortable ride will likely satisfy luxury-oriented family-car shoppers.

The TX’s towing capacity is acceptable but far from class-leading. The Volvo XC90 tops out at 5000 pounds, too, but the Audi Q7 can tug 7000 pounds, and the bigger Lexus GX550 has a 9096-pound rating.

The EPA estimates that the TX350 is good for 21 mpg city, 27 mpg highway, and 23 mpg combined with front-wheel drive; all-wheel drive models are rated for 20 mpg city, 26 mpg highway, and 23 mpg combined. First Row: The TX’s cabin is a little underwhelming to look at, but everything up front feels first class. The seats are cushy and heated, and leather upholstery is available. The TX's front seats are comfortable for long drives, and the commanding view out the windshield should satisfy SUV buyers.

Second Row: Depending on the trim level, shoppers have the option to swap the three-person bench for two heated and ventilated captain’s chairs. Both setups are comfortable and roomy enough for adults.

Third Row: Though the third row's bottom cushions are positioned close to the floor—like those in many a three-row SUV—the wayback is spacious enough for grown humans. Plus, the seatbacks recline.

Cargo Capacity: The TX has one of the largest cargo areas in the segment, offering 20 cubic feet of space behind the third row. There are also lots of receptacles for small items throughout the cabin. In our testing, we fit five carry-on suitcases behind the TX's third row and 18 with the third row stowed. With both the second and third rows stowed, we fit a total of 38.

We like the 14.0-inch infotainment display in the TX. It’s responsive and intuitive to use, though some settings are buried, and the touch-sensitive steering-wheel buttons are finicky. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto integration is standard, as are built-in navigation and a wireless smartphone charging pad. A 21-speaker Mark Levinson stereo and a head-up display are available.

Every TX rolls off the assembly line with a suite of driver-assistance features, including adaptive cruise control, lane-centering assist, and more.

For information about the TX's crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites.

The TX’s limited warranty is competitive, and its powertrain coverage surpasses many rivals’. Complimentary scheduled maintenance lasts for two visits, while the BMW X5 and the Volvo XC90 offer longer terms.

#4563. Meta-backed 250 MW solar farm breaks ground in Arkansas

Arkansas is getting another 250 megawatts (MW) of solar power, and Meta has signed up to buy it.

EDP Renewables North America (EDPR NA) broke ground on Cypress Knee Solar in Chicot County, in the southeastern corner of the state, on November 4. The solar farm is expected to be completed by 2028, bringing several hundred construction jobs and an estimated $25 million in county revenue over its lifetime.

Meta’s long-term power purchase agreement helps it work toward its pledge to match 100% of its annual electricity use with renewable energy generation. Don’t confuse that pledge with Meta powering its data centers with renewables around the clock, though – Facebook and Instagram’s parent company is also backing new gas plants to meet its growing power demand.

The companies announced the deal in May. Cypress Knee is their third clean-energy agreement, bringing the total capacity covered by Meta’s deals with EDPR NA to 545 MW.

“As energy demand continues to rise, projects like Cypress Knee Solar help strengthen grid reliability while creating jobs, generating meaningful local revenue, and delivering long-term benefits to the communities that host them,” said EDPR NA CEO Sandhya Ganapathy.

EDPR NA says it has already contributed more than $77,000 during project development, including money to restore the Lakeside High School greenhouse, resources for the Lakeside Robotics team, and funding for the Lake Village food pantry.

#4562. Uber Wants Thousands Of Robotaxis By 2027. Waymo Is Already There

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Uber has racked up a ton of autonomous vehicle partnerships, attempting to position itself as the key platform for driverless rides. And the company has no plans to slow down. On Tuesday, Uber said it wants to spend $10 billion to get 2,000 robotaxis into its global fleet by the end of 2027.

"Our autonomous strategy is entering an important new phase as more of our partners move from development and testing into driverless commercial service," CEO Dara Khosrowshahi said in written remarks shared alongside the company's third-quarter earnings.

Around half of those 2,000 robotaxis will be for the United States market, Uber said. The other half will be split up between Europe, Asia, and the Middle East. Uber says the self-driving fleet at that point will span 20 cities and include partnerships with May Mobility, Momenta, Zoox, Motional, and others. By the end of this year, Uber plans to have 700 robotaxis on its platform.

Here's the kicker, though: Even if Uber hits its goal by 2027, it will still be far behind Waymo, which is both a major competitor and, for now, a partner. Waymo, the most prominent robotaxi company in the world, already has a fleet of around 4,000 cars currently on the road, and it currently operates in 15 different U.S. cities.

Waymo aims to double its robotaxi count to 8,000 by the end of the year and hit 20,000 vehicles by the close of 2027, Semafor reported recently. So Uber would still be playing catch-up, big time.

And while users in cities like Atlanta have to use the Uber app to call a Waymo robotaxi, that's changing. Waymo co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana told Bloomberg on Wednesday that the company plans to end its exclusivity deal with Uber in Austin and Atlanta in January of 2028. It was “a little bit of a crapshoot,” she said, since Uber customers never knew if they were getting a robotaxi or a human driver.

Uber said its partners have committed to bringing 120,000 robotaxis onto its platform in the coming years, but hasn't put a timeframe on such a lofty goal. It says it's going to fund this fleet of robotaxis with its own earnings, but that it might have to “bring in third-party capital," once its self-driving fleet expands beyond 10,000 cars. Uber claims its gross bookings were up 20%, year-over-year, to the tune of $59.8 billion, so it's got a big book of business to fund its future projects. But with it splitting from Waymo, it's never been more important for the company to get its other partnership projects off the ground and expand them quickly.

#4561. Kia’s EV5 spotted with an updated design and a huge new infotainment display

Kia’s Sportage-sized electric SUV, the EV5, was spotted with a distinct new style and an overhauled interior, including a huge widescreen infotainment screen.

The EV5 is the fully electric SUV we want, but can’t have in the US. After launching it in China in 2023, Kia introduced the global version last year, which is now on sale in Europe, Canada, the UK, and other markets.

It has already been a big part of Kia’s comeback in China and is expected to become one of its best-selling EVs.

Kia appears to be preparing an updated version. A new EV5 model was recently spotted by ShortsCar in a South Korean parking garage without camouflage, and it’s expected to be the updated version.

You can see in the video that the design has changed quite a bit. Up front, the hood and headlights remain about the same, but new design elements like a black accent light are added.

It also features a unique bumper design, similar to that of the rugged EV5 WKNDR Concept Kia revealed last November at the Guangzhou Motor Show.

The biggest changes are inside, where the interior appears to be completely overhauled. Instead of the current large display screen spanning from the driver to the center, the new EV5 features a display that extends from the center to the passenger side.

There also appears to be an added slim display in front of the steering wheel. Since Hyundai has recently added a slim display to vehicles equipped with its Pleos infotainment system, the updated Kia EV5 is expected to feature the new setup.

However, this is still speculation and has not been confirmed. The center console has also changed. Instead of the physical buttons, it now has a cover, giving it a cleaner overall look.

According to a sticker on the back, the updated EV5 is set to launch in the Philippines. Given Kia initially launched the EV5 in China in 2023, it will be due for a facelift around 2027.

Kia has yet to confirm whether and when it will launch the updated EV5 in other global markets, such as Europe or Korea. It will likely arrive after the China-made version, like the current EV5. We should learn more details soon.

#4560. 8 Times Luffy Should Have Died in One Piece

Aden Carter is a Contributor at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2020. He specializes in lists and guides, with a focus on RPGs, horror games, survival horror, Soulslikes, cozy/sim games, and action-adventure titles. Before joining DualShockers, Aden contributed to GameRant, XDA, Gamepur, I

Luffy is the main protagonist of One Piece, which means that he has a degree of plot armor that will take him through to the end of the series. However, there are times where this plot armor has gone a bit far, saving Luffy’s life when it probably shouldn’t have.

We all know that Luffy is a lucky kid. He has escaped death on more than one occasion. He could have had his head chopped off, or he could have drowned at this point in the story, but somebody has stepped in or something has happened to prevent him from dying.

Even when we thought he was down for the count, he was saved, and managed to turn the tide of battle in his favor. He is a force that simply cannot be stopped.

The earliest time that Luffy should have died in One Piece is when he was taken out to sea by Higuma. Out in the ocean, the Lord of the Coast comes around, and Luffy gets thrown in the water.

His journey should have ended there, especially since the Lord of the Coast was about to completely devour him. Instead, Shanks stepped in, drove the Lord of the Coast away, and lost his arm in the process.

This is where Luffy’s journey should have possibly ended. After all, he was a rather impulsive young kid, and he still is to this day. However, like every entry on this list, there has been something that has prevented him from meeting his end.

There are some times where Luffy gets saved by other people, and then there are times where divine intervention has to play a role. That is, unless you want to work with the Monkey D. Dragon weather Devil Fruit theory.

While visiting Loguetown, Luffy manages to get himself capture by Buggy and his clownish crew, and as a result, Luffy is placed on the execution platform. At this point, it looks like Luffy is going to die, and he even calls out to everyone to say that he is dead.

Of course, divine intervention plays a role, because Buggy’s sword is struck by lightning, causing the platform to fall apart, leaving Luffy unscathed. As we know, Dragon is in Loguetown during this time, and it is theorized that he has a Devil Fruit that can control the weather, so maybe he saved his kid.

Early in Luffy’s pirating journey, he almost died several times, but one of the most memorable moments is his first interaction with Crocodile in Alabasta. While out in the desert, Luffy gets skewered by the then warlord of the sea.

It’s a very sudden hit, as Luffy is telling Crocodile to stop at the time, but the screen goes red, and we see Luffy hanging on the end of Crocodile’s hook. Crocodile then tosses him down into a sand pit to die.

Despite struggling to escape, Luffy can’t get out of the sand, and he is soon completely buried. He would have died here, but Nico Robin stepped in and saved his life. Still, it’s another moment that Luffy should have bit the dust.

Set sail and discover One Piece's darker characters like Sir Crocodile, Kaido, and Doflamingo.

As the vice warden of Impel Down, it is Magellan’s job to keep the prison running smoothly. Of course, Luffy completely ruined this when he entered Impel Down, and ultimately chose to pick a fight with the vice warden.

At this point in the story, Luffy wasn’t very strong. Well, at least not when you compare him to many of the other characters in the story. Going up against Magellan, Luffy ended up being coated in poison and was on his deathbed.

He should have died during this part of the story, but he was ultimately saved by the absolute legend that is Bon Clay. Bon Clay managed to get Luffy to Ivankov, who ultimately saved Luffy with hormone therapy which shortened his lifespan by 10 years. Still, this should have meant the end for the main character.

During the Whole Cake Island arc, Luffy decided to go toe-to-toe with Katakuri - Big Mom’s second son, and a man with a bounty of over 1 billion Berries. His signature move was the use of his observation haki to completely dodge attacks with his mochi powers.

During this fight, Luffy took hits nearly nonstop. It seemed like in every episode he was getting beaten up and there was no end in sight. Then, during episode 867, Luffy got hit by Katakuri’s spear in what was a devastating blow.

Many don’t realize that the hit was worse in the manga, and it tore open Luffy’s side. This, and many of the other hits, like being buried alive in mochi, should have ended Luffy’s pirating career, but he muscled his way through thanks to his plot armor.

Every One Piece fan is familiar with all the Emperors, but how do they rank against each other based on strength? Well, here's your answer.

One of the most one-sided fights in the entirety of One Piece is when Luffy foolishly tries to step up to Kaido in the early chapters of the Wano Country arc. At this point, Luffy fully believed he was ready to take on the yonko, but he was sorely mistaken.

Despite using his Gear 4 abilities, Luffy did nothing to Kaido, and instead got knocked out by one single swing from Kaido’s club. Ending the fight quickly without Kaido even needing to break a sweat.

It showcased just how far Luffy still needed to go to bridge the gap in power level. At this time, Kaido could have chosen to kill Luffy, but decided to imprison him instead. It’s a moment that Luffy should have died, but Kaido made a foolish choice by letting the boy live.

Luffy unlocking Gear 5 is one of the most memorable moments in the entire anime and manga. Seeing him go down, the light drain from his eyes, and then his hair turning white and awakening his Devil Fruit was something that was celebrated.

Unfortunately, it is another moment where I have to say that he should have died. Realistically, Kaido was too much for Luffy before he unlocked Gear 5.

While Luffy put up a good fight, he straight up died during his battle against Kaido. He even goes so far as to confirm that he died, but his fruit resurrected him in one of the ultimate displays of plot armor.

Before going forward, I want to give a major spoiler warning if you haven’t been caught up and been actively reading the Elbaf arc, as the anime has not reached this moment.

Now that you are aware of the consequences, Luffy received yet another degree of plot armor by surviving an attack that mirrors what happened during the Alabasta arc. Instead of Crocodile doing the impaling, this time it is Nerona Imu.

Imu comes down from his holy land of Mary Geoise, and Luffy is not strong enough to handle the fight. After taking numerous hits, Imu impales Luffy multiple times, leaving him for dead. He is saved by being in his Gear 5 form, and miraculously heals. This is a major use of plot armor, and one that might be a step too far.

Luffy has faced villains that ought to end his journey, but he always survives the face-off because of his willpower.

Created by Eiichiro Oda, One Piece follows Monkey D. Luffy and the Straw Hat Pirates on their journey across the seas.

#4558. Waymo And Uber's Robotaxi Partnership Is Ending

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

If you want to ride in a driverless Waymo in Austin or Atlanta, you can currently only do that via the Uber app thanks to an exclusive partnership between the two companies. That will change in 2028 because Waymo has decided to go solo in those two cities.

Waymo Co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana told Bloomberg on Wednesday that the company will exit its partnership with Uber in Austin and Atlanta starting in January 2028. The reason? Mawakana said the Uber app doesn’t guarantee a driverless ride. You can enable autonomous rides via settings in the Uber app, but the chances of one showing up depend on how many Waymos are actually nearby. If there's no Waymo nearby, riders are matched with human drivers.

Uber says it offered to add a dedicated robotaxi ride option through its service so that customers would match with driverless cars more easily, but Waymo reportedly declined that.

“In the early days, we would partner because we didn’t have the scale,” Mawakana told the outlet. "...in that partnering, it was a little bit of a crapshoot," she added.

Customers were now demanding a more consistent experience, Mawakana said. That’s why, starting in January 2028, Waymos in Austin and Atlanta will operate the same way they’ve been operating in over two dozen other U.S. cities: via Waymo’s own dedicated app. With that, current partner Uber will also become a direct rival in those two cities.

The whole point of this partnership was to help Waymo scale and give riders exposure to its cutting-edge driverless technology. Uber is the go-to ride-hail app for millions of riders already. The company also has vast experience in fleet operations and logistics.

Waymo, by comparison, is far smaller but is growing quickly. It’s a fully-owned subsidiary of Google parent Alphabet, which is valued at over $3.5 trillion as of writing. Waymo currently conducts over 500,000 paid driverless trips each week. It’s already operational in 15 U.S. cities and plans to add over a dozen more in the coming months. It's in a comfortable lead in the robotaxi race in the U.S., far ahead of Tesla and others.

It now seems more confident about going solo in Austin and Atlanta. However, it’s still partnering with Lyft for driverless rides in Nashville, although that partnership isn’t exclusive. Waymo also serves Nashville through its own app.

Uber also has grand ambitions when it comes to robotaxis. The company plans to have 700 robotaxis online by the end of this year and 2,000 by the end of 2027. It has emerged as a broker of robotaxi technology, inking deals with several companies including Rivian, Lucid, Wayve, and others to offer their driverless vehicles on the Uber app.
