#4530. Kia’s PV7 electric van stretches over 17 feet and seats 9

Kia is expanding its electric van lineup with the PV7, a larger PV5 sibling that can carry nine people or a whole lot of cargo.

The PV5, Kia’s first fully electric van from its Platform Beyond Vehicle (PBV) business, is proving to be a bigger hit than expected.

A year after it went on sale, the PV5 quickly became Europe’s most popular small electric van. In the first half of 2026, it was the top seller in its segment, accounting for 37% of electric C-segment van sales across Europe.

Next year, Kia will launch the PV7, the second electric van from its PBV business. Kia revealed the PV7 at IAA Transportation in Hanover, Germany, in September.

It’s based on the same E-GMP.S platform as the PV5, but the PV7 features a considerably longer wheelbase and stretched body, opening up more space inside.

The PV7 is over 17.5 ft long, measuring 5,350 mm long, 1,995 mm wide, and 1,990 mm high, with a 3,500 mm wheelbase. In comparison, the PV5 is just 4,695 mm long, 1,895 mm wide, and 1,915 mm tall, with a 2,995 mm wheelbase.

That’s even bigger than the Volkswagen ID. Buzz Long-Wheelbase (LWB), which measures 4,962 mm in length with a 3,239 mm wheelbase.

Like the PV5, the PV7 will initially be available in Passenger and Cargo body styles, but Kia plans to launch 23 different variants, or “top hats,” over the next few years.

It will be offered with two nickel-cobalt-manganese (NCM) battery packs: 71.5 kWh and 96.2 kWh. The Long Range Cargo model offers an all-electric WLTP range of over 460 km (285 miles). Even at full capacity, Kia said the new PV7 achieves nearly 400 km (248 miles) of range and still has 350 liters of trunk space.

A plena capacidad la nueva #PV7 consigue casi 400 km de autonomía y aún reserva 350 litros de maletero #Kia #KiaPV7 #MovementThatInspires pic.twitter.com/fzIvviYZuE

Front-wheel drive (FWD) will be standard at launch, but Kia plans to add an all-wheel drive (AWD) option later.

Depending on the configuration, the FWD electric powertrain delivers up to 268 horsepower (200 kW) and 309 lb-ft (420 Nm) of torque.

Thanks to its 800V architecture, the Kia PV7’s battery can charge from 10% to 80% in about 25 minutes with a 350 kW DC fast charger. It will be Kia’s first vehicle with two charging ports, including a front AC/DC port and an optional rear side AC port.

With vehicle-to-load (V2L) capabilities, it can serve as a mobile power source for tools, equipment, a campsite, or other external electronic devices.

The PV7 Cargo, designed for businesses, fleets, and logistics, is available in 2- and 3-seat configurations and offers up to 6.1 cubic meters of cargo space. The High Roof variant offers even more, with up to 8 cubic meters.

Maximum payload is up to 1,165 kg (2,568 lbs) for the Cargo Long and up to 1,200 kg (2,645 lbs) for the compact model.

The PV7 Cargo Long features a 550 mm loading height and, according to Kia, enough capacity for up to three Euro pallets (800 x 1,200 mm). An added heavy-duty mode adjusts the vehicle’s response to varying payloads to help maintain stability and control while driving.

Depending on the use, buyers can choose between full-open twin-swing tailgate doors or a lift-up tailgate.

The PV7 Passenger, on the other hand, is designed for personal use and families, or can also be used as a shuttle with room for up to nine passengers in the global version. In Korea, it will seat up to 11 passengers.

The 7-seater features Long-Rail Easy Remove Seats, enabling various interior seating configurations. The 9-seater variant, on the other hand, is available with or without a fourth row.

Inside, both versions feature Hyundai’s new Pleos Connect infotainment system, with 12.9″ and 14.6″ display screens and physical controls for commonly used functions.

The system runs Android Automotive OS, making it more like a smartphone with apps and customizable screens. It also includes Hyundai’s Gleo AI, an AI-powered in-car companion that can answer questions, control navigation or vehicle functions, and more.

26 minutes recharge might seem a bit lame for a 800V vehicle when the 400V Buzz will do it in 29, but this is still progress. And the PV7 will be pulling more absolute kW because it is a bigger, slightly less efficient vehicle.

Kia said the PV7 is based on a “Mobile Workspace” concept, with a layered dashboard and center console to optimize space.

The Kia PV7 Passenger and Cargo will go on sale in Korea and Europe in the second half of 2027. It will then roll out to new markets with new derivatives and conversions.

Kia will announce PV7 prices closer to its launch. In Korea, the PV5 Passenger and Cargo Compact starts at 45.9 million won ($34,000) and 41 million won ($30,000), respectively. In Germany, the PV5 Passenger 5-seater starts at €38,690 ($43,000).

The 2027 RAV4 Woodland gets a new suspension system that gives it an additional inch of ground clearance.

The 2027 Toyota RAV4 arrives with a collection of small tweaks that should add up to real improvements. Unfortunately, though not surprisingly, the new model year also comes with a slight price bump.

The 2027 RAV4 starts at $33,895 in front-drive LE trim, $36,695 for the front-drive SE, and $38,095 for the front-drive XLE Premium. Adding all-wheel drive to any of those trims incurs an additional $1600 cost. The AWD-only Woodland trim is up to $42,250, while the XSE is up to $43,495, and the Limited is up to $45,495. See all results for new 2027 Toyota RAV4 for sale near 10990

Every RAV4 thankfully now comes with a backup camera washer, and every AWD RAV4 gets Toyota’s Multi-Terrain Select modes. Plus, the Remote Connect trial is increasing from one year to five years, no matter the trim.

The bigger changes come when you zoom in. Woodland versions get redesigned all-weather floor and cargo mats. They also come with new suspension components, including springs, shocks, and jounce bumpers, that give them an additional inch of ground clearance. The first of the standard hybrid models will start arriving later this year, with plug-in models scheduled to launch in early 2027.

#4528. The BMW iX3 smashed its EPA range rating, driving well over 400 miles in a real-world test

BMW’s new iX3 outperformed the Volvo EX60 and Mercedes-Benz GLC EV, driving well over 400 miles during a real-world range test.

In a recent nationally representative survey, BMW found that Americans want more EV range than they actually need.

The study found that 73% consider 75 miles of range, or less, enough to cover their daily driving. Meanwhile, 42% said they would require at least 300 miles of range to consider an EV.

Another 53% said they would be more likely to consider an EV if it could add about 150 miles of range in 10 minutes.

BMW’s new iX3 checks all the boxes. Based on BMW’s sixth-generation (Gen6) eDrive 800V system, the 2027 iX3 50 xDrive delivers an EPA-estimated range of up to 434 miles (with 20″ summer tires).

With the 22″ summer tires, the iX3 50 xDrive has an EPA-estimated range of up to 392 miles. Still, plenty for at least a week of commuting.

It can also add 170-185 miles of range in 10 minutes with up to 400 kW DC fast charging. In everyday, real-world driving, it may drive even further than its official EPA numbers suggest.

During Edmunds‘ EV Range test, the 2027 BMW iX3 50 xDrive (with 22″ summer tires) drove 436 miles on a single charge, topping its EPA estimate of 392 miles by 44 miles.

The electric SUV was also more efficient than advertised. The iX3 achieved an energy consumption of 28.3 kWh per 100 miles, beating its EPA estimate of 32 kWh per 100 miles by roughly 11.6%.

BMW’s new iX3 is now the longest-range luxury electric SUV that Edmunds has tested, outperforming rivals including the 2027 Volvo EX60 (352 miles) and Mercedes-Benz GLC Electric (392 miles).

The Edmunds real-world range test is designed to provide a more accurate estimate of an EV’s range in everyday driving conditions.

It consists of 60% city and 40% highway driving with an average speed of 40 mph. The vehicle stays within 5 mph of the posted speed limit, and the climate control is set to auto at 72 degrees.

The 2027 BMW iX3 50 xDrive is available to order in Sport, M Sport, and M Sport Professional trims, priced from $61,500, $64,000, and $65,500, respectively.

The best cure for range anxiety is still actually driving an EV.

I've yet to have a conversation with someone who's EV dubious in which the answer to the question "how long are your gas stops on road trips" is anything less than 20 minutes - it's almost always at least 30.

Winter of course significantly impacts the calculations up north, which like everything brings us back to charging infrastructure buildout.

Not that it's going to happen anytime soon, could easily be never, but if battery swapping becomes a reliable thing I'd welcome the opportunity to change out battery size as needed.

Powered by a 108.7 kWh battery, the new iX3 with 20″ Summer Tires delivers up to 434 miles of range on a single charge.

With a charging rate of up to 400 kW, the new BMW iX3 can recharge from 10% to 80% in about 21 minutes, or add about 185 miles in 10 minutes.

Inside, the electric SUV features the Neue Klasse interior design. The setup includes BMW’s new Panoramic Vision, a full-length windshield display, and a 17.9″ central infotainment screen running the latest Operating System X. Buyers can also upgrade to the optional BMW 3D Head-Up Display.

#4527. BMW Is Giving New EV Buyers $500 In Free Charging

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

BMW's latest Neue Klasse EVs push the boundaries of range and charging speed. In short, they're some damn good electric cars. Now there's another reason to buy one: free charging.

BMW on Thursday said it's offering $500 in public charging credits for 2027 electric models. It applies to the i5, i7, and iX3, and is open to drivers who buy or lease. The benefits last for one year from the car's purchase date.

Here's how the $500 breaks down. BMW says $300 of it can be redeemed at more than 15 charging networks, including Ionna, Shell Recharge, ChargePoint, and EVgo. The other $200 only applies to Ionna locations. (BMW is one of the automakers backing Ionna.)

To access the funds, drivers need to set up an account through the BMW app. Once they do that and handle payment through BMW ChargingNetwork, credits are automatically applied to eligible charging purchases.

BMW is also offering buyers of 2027 EVs one free year of Ionna membership, which gets drivers 25% discounts on sessions at the fast-growing charging player.

If $500 in free charging sounds nice and you're considering these vehicles, I have one note of caution after getting behind the wheel of all three.

The i5 is a solid all-around EV. It drives well, looks familiar, and offers over 300 miles of range in some trims. But the i7 and iX3 are miles ahead in terms of onboard technology and specs. The latter models use BMW's Neue Klasse architecture and feature an overhauled digital interface with a wonderful "Panoramic Vision" display below the windshield. The iX3 offers over 400 miles of range and 400 kilowatt charging. Expect similar capabilities to trickle throughout BMW's lineup and into the next iteration of the i5 too.

#4525. Ocarina of Time Remake Director and Producer Credit Younger Developers for Vital Modern Perspective

Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.

The full remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has launched for the Nintendo Switch 2 today, and perhaps unsurprisingly, the response is quite positive. It’s still an excellent game after all these years, and the modern changes, both in its presentation and gameplay tweaks, improve the overall experience without detracting from the original’s timeless charm.

Hyrule has never looked better as they look in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake, and critics seem to agree!

It still feels like just yesterday when the original game launched for the Nintendo 64 in 1998, and a lot has changed in the industry since then. Heck, people who weren’t even born yet when that game came out are now working in game development, and apparently, some of those people also worked on the Ocarina of Time remake.

In an interview with The Verge, the remake’s director Hidemaro Fujibayashi and producer Eiji Aonuma, who was also the director on the original game, spoke about the vital perspectives that the team’s younger developers brought to the table in bringing the remake to life, including a few that have never even played the original. It was thanks in part to this next generation of devs that this fantastic meeting of gameplay history was able to take shape.

To paraphrase a bit of wisdom from a better writer than myself, the norms of the gaming industry are kind of like rings on a tree stump. Through various indicators in design, you can trace back the norms and common sense of game development through the ages.

The norms of the gaming industry are kind of like rings on a tree stump.

The original Ocarina of Time, while a fantastic game, is a lot different from today’s norms in its visual and mechanical approaches, and needs to be recognized as such to create a proper modern remake. If the only people working on the remake were those who worked on and/or played the original, they would’ve just made the original again. This, as Fujibayashi and Aonuma explain, is why having younger developers on the team was so important.

Eiji Aonuma and the development team for the Ocarina of Time remake discussed how one of the original's infamous dungeons is being improved.

Despite some of them not having played the original, the younger developers on the team understood in the broad sense what made its formula work, and so strove for simple, careful additions and subtractions to bring it a little more in line with modern sensibilities.

“I feel confident that they weren’t necessarily pursuing something new for the sake of novelty when it might be unneeded and clutter the experience,” Fujibayashi said. “They’re looking for elegance. Only what is needed, only what was important in the original, and how to carry that forward as their focus.”

Aonuma and Fujibayashi’s work on the remake alongside the rest of their development team really helped to illustrate to them how much has changed in the game development pipeline since Aonuma’s heyday on the original Ocarina of Time nearly 30 years ago.

“We used to have maybe just one person designing the backgrounds, and that’s something that you couldn’t do nowadays,” Aonuma said. “A lot of the process is not so different compared to the N64 days, but the scale [is different]: There’s a lot more time involved, a lot more people involved, and because of that it can be harder to manage these teams.”

Fujibayashi also worked as the director for the modern, wide-open Zelda games like Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom, which are much different beasts compared to more streamlined, linear approach of Ocarina of Time. Fujibayashi recalls being fascinated with Nintendo’s early approaches to the new conundrums of 3D back in the day, particularly with the advent of the Z-targeting system. “The solutions are something that still stick with me as a foundation for when I create 3D games,” he said.

At the end of the interview, Aonuma reflected on how diversity in game design is what gives the Zelda franchise its staying power, and how this modern take on Ocarina of Time is a good example of its ability to mix things up as much (or as little) as necessary.

“We’ve had opportunities to add to the playbook of Zelda, if you will, and the language of development,” he said. “You get to see the progression of these ideas across the franchise. And now, working with younger staff on this remake, we’re having the opportunity to bring in additional new ideas. I really look forward to the future and what’s possible coming from the new staff.”

#4523. Gas Prices Got You Down? This 261-MPG Volkswagen Solves That—For $140,000

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

In 2013, VW launched one of the most fascinating experiments in fuel efficiency ever made. The Volkswagen XL1 took 12 years to develop and ended up costing a whopping $150,000 at the time. However, as an engineering exercise, it was brilliant. And since VW only made 250, it's even rarer than a Bugatti Veyron from the same era.

If you're looking for an extreme answer to high gas prices, today's your lucky day. There's currently an XL1 in the Netherlands up for auction on Catawiki. The 2016 model up for grabs has just over 1,000 miles on the odometer and is apparently in excellent condition inside and out.

The XL1 project was spearheaded by Ferdinand Piech, VW's top boss at the time. Not known to ever give up on his lofty, ambitious goals, Piech fought for 12 years, and through several iterations, to finally achieve his "one liter" car, something that could burn just one liter of fuel per every 100 km. VW pulled out all the stops to make it extraordinarily efficient; the result was something closer to a supercar than a Toyota Prius.

That teardrop-shaped body is made from carbon fiber, as is its chassis, saving weight. It debuted a full year before BMW's i3, an EV/PHEV which only had a carbon chassis but a plastic body. The car has butterfly doors and two seats that are offset to optimize the car's aerodynamic shape.

Power comes from an 800cc, two-cylinder, turbo-diesel engine behind the driver—this makes it mid-engine, like a supercar—plus a plug-in hybrid system centered around a 5.5 kilowatt-hour battery. The plug-in hybrid powertrain wasn't originally planned, and didn't come about until near the end of its development, so it needed a massive 50-pound removable charging box in the trunk so you could plug it in.

With a funky hybrid powertrain, a curb weight of just 1,852 pounds, and a drag coefficient of just 0.189, the XL1 was capable of an EU-tested 0.9 liters per 100 km, which equates to 261 mpg. It can also travel 31 miles on battery power alone, registering an insane efficiency of 6.2 miles per kWh, about double today's more conventional EVs. VW said at the time of the XL1's launch that it only needed about 8 horsepower to sustain a steady 62 mph.

The main downside is performance: It only makes 68 horsepower, so it takes almost 13 seconds to get to 60 mph.

This specific car up for auction is expected to fetch around $140,000, according to the auction house. So even with its incredible fuel economy and currently outrageous fuel prices, the XL1's financial breakeven point is still a long ways away. Plus, it runs on diesel, which has seen even steeper price spikes than regular gas. A used EV cuts you off from the gas station entirely, and is a better all-around choice of course.

But for someone who wants an amazing piece of automotive history, the XL1 could be worth the price. Plus, it'll sip on fuel like no other for many of your daily errands—and look cool doing it.

All Cybertrucks boast impressive 35-degree approach and 28-degree departure angles, so the Tesla pickup should be a formidable off-road machine. On the road, the big Cybertruck feels more agile than expected. We drove a Cyberbeast and found its combination of rear-wheel steering and variable-ratio steer-by-wire tech made for easy maneuvering in urban environments.

In Comparison: The tri-motor Cyberbeast's 2.6-second 60-mph time makes it quicker than the quad-motor Rivian R1T, which needed 3.0 seconds to get to the same speed. Even more impressive, the Cyberbeast's 60-mph time matches that of the Chevy Corvette C8 Z06.

The Premium and Cyberbeast models have a maximum towing capacity of 11,000 pounds, while the base trim is rated to tug 7500 pounds. Payload varies by model and tire choice, but an all-terrain-shod Cybertruck Premium can haul the most, carrying 2500 pounds in its six-by-four-foot composite cargo bed.

The Tesla Cyberbeast's battery capacity is approximately 122.4 kWh. Tesla claims the base model can recoup 132 miles in 15 minutes when hooked up to a Supercharger. In the same timeframe, the Premium model can restore 137 miles while the Cyberbeast adds 135. In our testing, it took 50 minutes to charge the Cyberbeast's battery from 10 to 50 percent.

Since the Cybertruck is technically considered a heavy-duty pickup truck by the EPA's standards, Tesla isn't required to report fuel-economy figures to the government agency. We observed 55 MPGe in mixed driving with a Cyberbeast.

First Row: Those who thought the Tesla Model 3's interior was minimalistic will relive that reaction when they see the Cybertruck's spartan cabin. The base model boasts heated front seats and a single central touchscreen, while the other two have seat heating and ventilation, plus a second screen for rear-seat passengers.

Second Row: Headroom is surprisingly generous in the rear seat given the truck's dramatically sloped roofline, but riders over six feet tall may find it snug.

Cargo Capacity: In our testing, we found that the truck's front trunk (frunk) holds just one carry-on suitcase, but the interior will fit 22 with the rear seats folded. The Cybertruck's cargo bed offers 121 cubic feet of volume, and inside the bed is a hidden underfloor storage compartment that’s large enough to fit an additional suitcase.

Every Cybertruck has a big 18.5-inch touchscreen mounted in the center of the dashboard. In the Premium and Cyberbeast, there's also a 9.4-inch touchscreen on the back of the center console for rear-seat passengers. SiriusXM satellite radio is included, as is a Wi-Fi hotspot, but drivers hoping for Apple CarPlay and Android Auto will be disappointed, as those features do not appear in any Tesla model.

Every Cybertruck comes standard with Tesla's controversial Autopilot driving feature. The brand's Full Self-Driving (supervised) system is optional. Neither system yet enables fully autonomous driving, something Tesla has long promised. The company also provides other, more basic driver-assistance technology.

For information about the Cybertruck's crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites.

Tesla provides a comprehensive warranty on its current models; however, it doesn't include any complimentary maintenance.

#4519. Tesla Is Killing The Cybertruck To Make Room For More Robotaxis

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

The controversial Tesla Cybertruck electric pickup will be retired next year, CEO Elon Musk confirmed on X. The angular truck went on sale at the end of 2023 and instantly became a social statement—for better or worse.

Production of the Cybertruck will start winding down next summer at the company’s Texas Gigafactory, and the extra floor space will be used to build more Cybercabs.

The unpainted truck had a short burst in popularity at the beginning of its production run, but interest fizzled, and sales never reached the potential that Musk and Tesla had envisioned back in 2019, when the vehicle was first presented as a concept.

In this year’s third quarter, the Cybertruck amassed 4,323 sales, according to data from Cox Automotive. From January through September, sales totaled 11,586 units. Tesla doesn’t break out individual sales figures for the Cybertruck, but industry estimates put the vehicle’s overall deliveries at roughly 70,000.

That’s a far cry from the hundreds of thousands of sales recorded every quarter by the Model 3 and Model Y. It’s also another reminder that electric pickups haven’t quite taken off as their manufacturers had hoped, and Tesla is now taking the fall, just like Ford did with the F-150 Lightning, which went the way of the dodo last year after lackluster sales and ballooning costs.

There’s no denying that you either love or hate the Cybertruck, just like there’s no denying that Tesla dared to do things like no other car manufacturer before it. Sure, some might argue that the angular EV looks like an unpolished fridge, but it brought steer-by-wire and a 48-volt low-voltage architecture to the masses. Whether or not they’ll be adopted by other companies is another story, though.

At roughly the same time as Elon Musk’s announcement that Cybertruck production would wind down in the middle of 2027, Tesla stopped taking orders for the entry-level Dual-Motor All-Wheel Drive version of the model, leaving just the Premium and Cyberbeast trims available to order on the automaker’s website.

Additionally, the price of the remaining models has been increased. The Premium AWD model now starts at $92,490, up from $89,990, while the top Cyberbeast now costs $102,490, up from $99,990. The most recent price bumps come after a similar move in August.

#4515. Over A Quarter Of BMW, Mini, And Rolls-Royce Models Sold In Q3 Had A Plug

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

The BMW Group, which operates the BMW, Mini, and Rolls-Royce car brands, saw 20% of its global vehicle sales in the third quarter represented by all-electric models. Adding plug-in hybrids increases the electrified models’ share to 27.4%, the company said in its latest earnings report.

From the beginning of the year through September, EVs have accounted for 18.4% of the three automakers’ total sales worldwide, with PHEVs raising the figure to 26.1%.

Despite the promising numbers, the automotive group clearly has a regionalization problem on its hands. Europe is leading the way by a wide margin, with 34.7% of sales represented by EVs and 46.9% by all electrified models.

Meanwhile, over in the United States, just 4.7% of BMW, Mini, and Rolls-Royce models sold were EVs. That’s a huge difference, and it puts the U.S. at the bottom of the BMW Group’s list for electrification. By comparison, Chinese EV sales amounted to 6.5%, while the Asia-Pacific, Eastern Europe, Middle East, and Africa regions totaled 18% EV sales.

The only thing that saves the day for the company’s electrified lineup in the U.S. is plug-in hybrids, which, together with EVs, had an 11.4% share in the third quarter. It’s also worth noting that the new iX3 and i3 models are just starting to trickle down to American dealers, and the U.S. also doesn’t get the electric iX2 and iX2 that Europeans have access to. The updated i7 is also on its way, but that has always been a low-volume car that never made a meaningful impact on the company’s sales reports.

What’s more, even though one in every five BMW Group models was all-electric in Q3, the company’s year-to-date numbers aren’t so promising. Globally, the group sold 314,552 EVs and 131,653 PHEVs from January through September, a 5.1% decrease compared to the same period last year. EVs saw a 2.7% drop, while PHEV sales declined 10.3%.

The only positive number in the company’s electrification Excel sheets has to do with how many EVs were sold in comparison to everything else in the portfolio. In the first three quarters of 2026, the share of EV sales within the BMW Group reached 18.4%, up from last year’s 18%.

Things should improve once the iX3 and i3 are widely available everywhere in the world, but they’re not guaranteed to be a success in the U.S., where policy whiplash has severely slowed the adoption of all-electric vehicles.

After opening pre-orders for the new 5-seat luxury electric SUV last week, Li Hui, Denza’s general manager, said the results so far “have been excellent.”

According to Li, the Denza N8 is “definitely the most anticipated luxury SUV of the year.” Using BYD’s second-generation Blade Batteries, the Denza N8 EV has a pure electric CLTC range of up to 1,003 km (623 miles) on a single charge.

That’s just as much as the N8 plug-in hybrid (PHEV) it’s replacing, which offered a combined CLTC range of 1,003 km (623 miles) on a full tank of gas and a full charge.

While Li confirmed last week that the new EV variant would go on sale in November, he didn’t give a specific date.

Now, it’s official. Denza announced on its Weibo page on Friday that the launch event for the Denza N8 EV will be held on November 12, 2026.

BYD is still offering a limited-time promo that includes a 5,000 RMB credit for those who place a reservation with a 2,000 RMB ($200) deposit.

The Denza N8 measures 5,150 mm long, 1,999 mm wide, and 1,820 mm high, with a 3,075 mm wheelbase. That’s slightly longer than the Kia EV9 and Hyundai IONIQ 9.

Like most of its new luxury vehicles, the Denza N8 is loaded with BYD’s latest software and technology.

Added premium features include zero-gravity seating in all rows, a three-spoke steering wheel, wireless phone chargers, and ambient lighting.

The electric SUV is equipped with a roof-mounted LiDAR to support BYD’s God’s Eye 5.0 intelligent driving assistance system, plus its DiSus-A intelligent air suspension system.

BYD has yet to announce prices for the Denza N8 EV, but it will likely be slightly less than the N8L, an extended version that starts at 299,800 RMB ($45,000).

Covering the video games industry since 2017, with experience in news, articles, and reviews. Currently a writer at DualShockers and gaming magazines.

Remember when survival horror games were all about fixed camera angles, chunky polygonal characters, limited ammunition, and doors that took an unnecessarily long time to open?

Well, someone decided to bring all of that back with an unexpected project inspired by Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie – and fans (including myself) are absolutely loving it!

Called Zach Cregger's RESIDENT EVIL: The Video Game, this unofficial fan project was created by the developer and game producer Stefano Cagnani, who already created similar projects in the past for classic films such as Alien, Dawn of the Dead, The Crow, and more. And you can play it for free on itch.io right now by checking out the project on this page!

It is currently available for PC and reimagines the director's movie as a classic PlayStation 1 survival horror experience. And honestly, if you're anything like me and have a soft spot for the franchise's early days, this might be right up your alley.

There are several Resident Evil titles that deserve to be remade after Resident Evil Veronica.

As its name suggests, the project takes the movie's premise and gives it a nostalgic makeover, complete with everything you'd expect from a late-'90s Resident Evil game. So yes, we are talking fixed camera angles, tank controls, low-poly graphics, dark environments, scarce ammunition, and even those iconic close-ups of doors opening as you move between areas.

However, don't expect to experience the entire movie just yet. The current version only covers its opening sequence, following the snowy road until the protagonist reaches the farm – but it already features the appearance of one of the movie's most terrifying creatures.

Called Zach Cregger's RESIDENT EVIL: The Video Game, this unofficial fan project was created by the developer and game producer Stefano Cagnani, who already created similar projects in the past for classic films such as Alien, Dawn of the Dead, The Crow, and more.

What makes this project so interesting is how lovingly it recreates the atmosphere of classic survival horror. It's a wonderful love letter not only to Cregger's movie (which finally broke the franchise's curse of not having a genuinely good live-action film – sorry, Milla Jovovich!), but also to the early Resident Evil games that made so many of us fall in love with the series.

If you are a fan of horror titles, there are plenty of old games that should be brought back, as they were something great.

Although the project was released a few days ago, it's only now starting to gain more attention, with fans sharing gameplay footage and streaming their experiences online. And judging by the reactions, Stefano might have something pretty special on his hands.

One player was already asking for more, commenting, "Full game needs to be released as soon as possible." Another praised its nostalgic atmosphere, saying, "This looks actually pretty sick. [It] takes me back to the 90s style of Resident Evil." Not everyone was simply celebrating the throwback, though. One particularly amusing comment praised the project while taking a little jab at the movie's humor: "did they remove the constant jokes and constant humor? If so, I'm sold!"

Well, I guess you can't please everyone! Regardless, it's lovely to see a fan project capturing the attention of Resident Evil fans, especially one that understands just how much atmosphere and a few well-placed camera angles can do for a survival horror experience. So, if you've been missing the days of wandering through dark corridors with barely enough ammunition to defend yourself, this free little project might be exactly what you need.

The Lotus Evija is a marvel of modern engineering, and not just for its astonishing acceleration, its stunning looks, or its incredible 2012 horsepower rating. A torque-vectoring all-wheel-drive system helps get that enormous power to the asphalt, resulting in what we estimate will be a 1.8-second 60 mph time. This hypercar’s cabin also positions all of its key controls around the driver and minimizes distractions by forgoing traditional infotainment and driver-assistance features altogether. Unfortunately, even the mega-rich can't drive one in America outside of a race track, as it's not legal for U.S. roads.

The Evija rolls into 2027 without any significant updates.

If this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying new.

The Evija's electric powertrain is comprised of four electric motors that generate a total output of 2012 horsepower and 1257 pound-feet of torque. That's almost double the horsepower provided by hypercars such as the Aston Martin Valkyrie. A single-speed automatic transmission governs it all, sending power to all four wheels. The car's relatively light curb weight is designed to optimize handling. The company claims the Evija weighs in at around 4200 pounds, making it supposedly the lightest EV hypercar to enter production.

The car's performance can be customized via five driving modes: Range, City, Tour, Sport, and Track. On our test drive of the Evija, we were gobsmacked by its awesome power and nimble demeanor. Unlike some performance EVs that have a rock-solid brake pedal feel, the Evija’s carbon-ceramic brakes provide astonishing stopping power and can be easily modulated. We also enjoyed its hydraulic power steering, which provided more feedback than almost every other high-powered EV currently available.

In Comparison: We estimate that the Evija will be capable of hitting 60 mph in just 1.8 seconds. That puts it in contention with our estimated 60-mph time for the equally exotic electric Rimac Nevera. One car that actually went that quickly is the 1250-hp hybrid Chevrolet Corvette ZR1X, which scorched its way to 60 mph in 1.8 seconds in our track testing.

Lotus claims that the Evija takes a mere 18 minutes to juice from 10 to 80 percent on a 350-kW charger. Lotus said it expects its hypercar to deliver a 195-mile driving range. When we drove a prototype Evija on track back in 2021, we emptied its fully charged battery in just 15 minutes. That figure might be improved for the production model, but full-tilt driving is sure to zap range significantly.

Since the Evija isn't street-legal, it's unlikely the EPA will estimate its fuel efficiency. We're sure exactly none of the über-rich car enthusiasts who will be able to buy one will care.

First Row: The Lotus Evija seats two passengers, and its cabin is accessed via a pair of dihedral doors. The Evija's electrically adjustable front seats feature a carbon-fiber shell and thick pads swathed in microfiber. The driver can manually adjust the tilt and length of the steering column, and there are two bespoke storage spaces placed close to the occupants' hip points.

Cargo Capacity: There is no trunk or frunk in the Evija, and storage opportunities are limited inside the cabin. This is not a car for road trips or grocery-getting.

All Evijas come with tech features such as Bluetooth connectivity and an infotainment system. In front of the steering wheel, there's a digital display that provides the driver with pertinent information like battery charge and remaining range. This is the car's only screen.

The Evija comes with Apple CarPlay and Android Auto capability, and Lotus has installed an onboard modem that facilitates connection to the cloud. A smartphone app is available that allows drivers to monitor the Evija from any location, checking on things such as battery charge status and driving range.

The Evija offers no traditional driver-assistance features such as lane-keeping assist, adaptive cruise control, or automated emergency braking.

Lotus doesn't offer a particularly impressive limited or powertrain warranty. The company also doesn't include any complimentary scheduled maintenance.

#4510. China's World-Beating Supercar Just Hit 312 MPH

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

A Chinese EV is officially the fastest production car in the world and the first production car in history to break the 500 kilometers per hour (310 miles per hour) barrier. BYD’s Yangwang U9 Xtreme, a two-door electric hypercar, reached 503.17 kph (312.6 mph) on a public road in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, on November 1.

As a reminder, the U9 Xtreme was already the world’s fastest car, after it reached 496.22 kph (308.3 mph) back in September 2025, but the Chinese automaker had already set its sights last year on breaking the 500 kph barrier—something that no other production car has ever managed.

The latest and most impressive record happened on a roughly 10-kilometer (6.2-mile) stretch of the E11 road in Abu Dhabi’s Al Dhafra Region, which was closed to public traffic. German racing driver Marc Basseng, the same driver who delivered the previous record, was behind the wheel and needed four runs over the course of two days to set the new record.

The first two runs happened on October 31, when the maximum speed was 490 kph (304.4 mph). Engineers made adjustments to the vehicle’s aerodynamics, suspension settings, and tire pressures to improve stability and performance. Then, on the last run of the second day, the Racelogic recorder made the 503.17 kph (312.6 mph) run official.

According to Guinness World Records, the Yangwang U9 Xtreme now holds the records for the highest speed achieved by a production car and an electric production car in a single-direction run. The FIA also confirmed the achievement on its website.

That last part is particularly interesting because the usual way of breaking records involves two separate runs in opposite directions to account for elevation change, wind speed, and any potential breakdown. BYD went for a single run in a single direction, which could make companies like Rimac, Bugatti, and Koenigsegg raise an eyebrow and challenge BYD’s result.

Nevertheless, going over 500 kph in a production car—albeit a limited-production model—is immensely impressive, especially considering that it’s an EV. BYD plans to make just 30 units of the U9 Xtreme, which is the most powerful and fastest version of the U9 supercar. Powered by four electric motors totaling 2,977 horsepower, the Xtreme uses a 1,200-volt lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery pack that can discharge at a 30C rate. A set of semi-slick GitiSport e-GTR2 Pro tires keeps the car on the road and provides stopping power, helped by titanium calipers and carbon-ceramic rotors.

#4509. EVgo opens its first Tesla Superchargers, with hundreds more planned

EVgo has opened its first Supercharger station, and it’s in a Chicago grocery store parking lot. The site has 12 fast-charging stalls with both NACS and CCS plugs, and it’s the first of hundreds of Tesla Supercharger stalls EVgo plans to add across the US.

The 325 kW “EVgo Superchargers” are at Riverside Square & River’s Edge, at 3145 S Ashland Avenue. EVgo’s August announcement cited up to 500 kW for the Supercharger rollout.

The Chicago location features Magic Dock technology, which means both NACS and CCS vehicles can charge without an adapter. Drivers of compatible non-Tesla EVs can start a session through the Tesla app. If you drive a Tesla, the charging station shows up in the car’s navigation and Trip Planner. Other EVgo fast chargers with NACS plugs have been showing up in Tesla navigation since early September if you turn on third-party charging.

“By serving both Tesla and non-Tesla NACS drivers, we’re doubling EVgo’s addressable market and continuing to meet EV drivers where they are and where they want to charge,” said Badar Khan, EVgo CEO.

EVgo owns the Superchargers and self-brands them, and Tesla runs and maintains them. The first sites will be at Regency Centers shopping plazas with grocery stores.

EVgo is also adding NACS plugs to its regular fast-charging network, a rollout it started in 2025. The company aims to have 500 of those stalls across the US by the end of 2026, with Supercharger stalls counted separately. Over the next two years, it plans to put at least one NACS plug at every EVgo site built in 2023 or later.

If you want something speedier, consider the turbocharged version of the Mazda CX-30 Turbo, which needed only 6.2 seconds to hit 60 mph in our testing.

According to the EPA, the Envista is estimated to return 28 mpg city, 32 mpg highway, and 30 mpg combined. On our 75-mph highway fuel economy test route, which is an integral part of our extensive testing regimen, the 2025 Envista delivered precisely on its 32-mpg promise. For more information about the Envista's fuel economy, visit the EPA's website.

First Row: Inside, the Envista offers a cabin that's roomy for four. Interior materials aren't luxury grade, but compared to rivals such as the Mitsubishi Outlander Sport, the Buick more than measures up. It also offers plenty of convenience features and desirable tech gadgetry, including a large dashboard screen that houses both the digital gauge display and the infotainment touchscreen. The top-spec Avenir gets the fanciest interior and rises to near the top of the class in terms of ambiance, but this is no competitor to more expensive models from Audi, BMW, or Mercedes-Benz.

Second Row: The Envista’s chic coupe-like roofline doesn't noticeably cut into rear-seat headroom.

Cargo Capacity: Important for a vehicle where practicality is a given, it can haul 20 cubic feet of gear, and 42 cubic feet of stuff with the rear seats folded. In our testing, the Envista fit six carry-on suitcases in its trunk and 19 cases in total with the rear seats folded.

The Envista's dashboard consists of two digital displays under one piece of glass: an 8.0-inch gauge cluster and a second 11.0-inch touchscreen infotainment interface. There is also a separate panel for climate controls below a center-mounted dash vent. The Envista uses Buick's most up-to-date software, and it includes standard wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto and an onboard Wi-Fi hotspot. All trims come with a six-speaker stereo.

All Envistas are equipped with a comprehensive set of driver-assistance features, including automatic high-beam headlamps, adaptive cruise control, and automated emergency braking.

For information about the Envista’s crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites.

Buick's standard warranty package matches that of many of the Envista's key rivals but pales in comparison with the plans of the Hyundai Kona, which provides far lengthier terms as well as three years of complimentary scheduled maintenance.

#4507. New method measures microplastics in the air using an uncrewed aerial system

Microplastics have been found in our bodies and the food we eat—and even in remote environments around the world, including seawater and ice in the Arctic. Despite their prevalence, little is known about how they move through the atmosphere. New CIRES-led research, which demonstrates a new method for sampling microplastics in the atmosphere using an uncrewed aerial system (UAS), aims to change that. The findings are published in the journal Scientific Reports.

#4505. How Far Can Your EV Go After It Says It’s Empty?

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

What do you do when your EV’s range prediction shows zero and the nearest charger is still a few miles away? Will you make it? In a Tesla Model Y Long Range, you’d pull in with miles to spare, while in an Xpeng P7+, you’d have been on the phone with roadside assistance, even if the Xpeng goes farther on a full charge.

That’s one of the more revealing findings from AUTOBEST’s 2026 ECOBEST Challenge. All 15 EVs that took part in the group test kept moving after their dashboards showed empty, averaging 10 miles (16 km) before they stopped. The Leapmotor B10 led with 19.9 miles (32 km), about a mile ahead of the Model Y. At the other end, the Xpeng barely managed 0.6 miles.

Car journalists drove these production-spec EVs in convoy near Milan, Italy, on a set route containing a mix of city streets, country roads and highways. A lead car set the pace, and drivers traded cars every 19 miles (30 km) to level out potential differences in driving style.

Only the driver was aboard each car; all vehicles were set to their standard (not Eco) mode, with climate control on and tires set to the recommended pressures. Temperatures ranged from 68–77°F (20–25°C).

The final stretch took place at Quattroruote’s Vairano proving ground. When a car’s dashboard showed either zero remaining range or 0% battery charge, its driver kept going until the car could no longer move under its own power. They measured the distance between those two points to see how far each EV could still go.

They used a Zeekr 7GT as a support vehicle to quickly reach drivers whose EVs had stopped. Using its vehicle-to-load (V2L) function, it drew electricity from its own battery pack to get the other vehicles moving again, eliminating the need for a dedicated EV road assistance van.

When your EV says it’s empty, it means you’ve used up the range the car promised you. You may still have enough energy to drive a little farther, since all EVs have a buffer. As the state of charge goes down, the voltage in the battery cells also drops. Before it goes too low, which can damage the cells, the car cuts power to the motor.

So, even when an EV shows 0% and can’t move, some charge remains in the pack—the car won’t let it go completely flat.

Zero percent is the car’s estimate of its remaining usable charge. The range estimate approximates how far that energy will take you. Interestingly, those numbers don’t necessarily have to coincide; they can hit zero at different times. For instance, in one range test, the Tesla Model 3 still showed 2 miles (3.2 km) of range when the state of charge dropped to 0%. It went another 31 miles (50 km) after that point.

AUTOBEST published the distance each car covered after zero, but its results table doesn’t give the usable energy remaining at that moment or the speed each car maintained afterward. So we can say the Leapmotor drove 32 times as far as the Xpeng past empty, but that doesn’t mean its battery had 32 times the current reserve.

#4504. Apollo’s newest electric scooter is also its lowest-cost yet

Apollo has spent the last several years carving out a spot for itself toward the more premium end of the electric scooter market. Now the company is trying something different: going after the mass market with its least expensive model yet.

The new Apollo Dash carries a $699 MSRP, but is launching at $599 as part of the company’s Black Friday sale running through November 30. More importantly, Apollo says the Dash isn’t intended to simply be a stripped-down budget scooter, but rather a way to bring much of its existing technology down to a lower price point.

The scooter uses a 48V electrical system powering a 600W nominal, 1,200W peak-rated Bosch motor, with a top speed of 20 mph (32 km/h). Its 480Wh battery is rated for up to 25 miles (40 km) of range in Eco mode.

Apollo also claims the 48V architecture avoids limiting motor power to anemic levels as the battery drains, meaning riders shouldn’t experience the same increasingly sluggish performance toward the bottom of the battery that can occur on some lower-cost scooters.

At 43 lb (19.5 kg), the Dash is reasonably portable, though getting the weight and price down comes with an important compromise: there’s no suspension. Apollo also caps rider weight at 220 lb (100 kg), and points heavier riders or those regularly tackling rough roads and hills toward the more expensive Apollo Go instead.

Despite the lower price, there’s still a surprisingly long feature list. The Dash gets IP66 water resistance, self-healing tubeless tires, regenerative braking, built-in turn signals, Apollo’s Beam stem light, NFC unlocking, Apple Find My integration, and connectivity with the Apollo smartphone app.

Apollo says it put the frame through 10,000 km (6,200 miles) of durability validation before shipping production units. A beta test program also accumulated 1,002 miles over 144 rides without any reported punctures or maintenance issues. Beta riders averaged 19 miles (30 km) per ride while finishing with 29% battery remaining, according to Apollo.

Perhaps the bigger story here, though, is where Apollo is positioning the Dash. The company says 52% of its customers previously owned scooters from brands including Segway, NIU, and Xiaomi, but historically moving up to an Apollo often meant crossing the $1,000 mark.

At $599, the Dash appears designed to get those riders into Apollo’s ecosystem much earlier – while also putting the company squarely into competition with the mass-market scooters it previously sat above.

And for those wanting a bit more power or features, Apollo’s more upmarket models are on sale now as part of early Black Friday promotions.

Jeep has an electric alternative to its Wrangler SUV with the 2027 Recon EV. The Recon wears a similarly boxy design to the Wrangler, its roof opens, and its doors come off for the feeling of open-air freedom that is quintessential Jeep. A pair of electric motors pumps out a healthy 670 horsepower, and acceleration is brisk.

However, we’d happily trade some of that acceleration for additional driving range, which runs 222 miles per charge for the Moab trim and 240 miles per charge for the upscale Overland. If you can live with below-average driving range, the Recon EV excels as an off-roader and can be used like any other boxy mid-size SUV on pavement—meaning it's relatively practical and easy to live with.

Expert Tip: If you want an electric Jeep and don’t need the Recon’s ground clearance and off-road capability, the Wagoneer S is a more luxurious option with more driving range.

Compare the 2027 Jeep Recon EV with the top vehicles in this segment with our new compare tool.

A luxurious Overland trim joins the lineup for 2027. This more road-friendly variant is said to have a slightly longer 240-mile driving range estimate, and it wears a more upscale look due to body-colored fender flares and 20-inch alloy wheels. Elsewhere, a NACS charging port replaces last year’s CCS connector, so replenishing the battery at Tesla Superchargers is now possible.

If this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying new.

The Jeep Recon EV utilizes a pair of electric motors, with one drive unit mounted in the front and another in the rear. They produce a combined output of 670 horsepower—serious muscle that delivers impressive acceleration.

In addition to standard all-wheel drive, the Recon touts features that should make it a stout off-road performer as well: an electric locking differential, 9.1 inches of ground clearance, and a Select-Terrain traction management system with rock, sand, and snow drive modes. When we drove the Recon, we found it to be entertainingly quick on the road, with better ride quality and handling when compared to the gas-powered Wrangler. Off-road, its touchy throttle and sensitive brakes make it more difficult to pilot, but it’s plenty capable in the dirt.

In Comparison: A 3.5-second 60 mph dash is mighty quick for a mid-size SUV, especially one focused on off-road capabilities.

The Recon EV is capable of towing up to 3300 pounds when equipped with the Trailer Tow Group package. That's a bit less than the 3,500-pound rating for the Wagoneer S.

With its 100.5-kWh battery pack fully juiced, the EPA rates the Moab trim to deliver 222 miles of all-electric driving range. The Overland trim is estimated at 240 miles. In our real-world 75-mph highway test, the Moab achieved a disappointing result of just 160 miles.

The Recon employs a 400-volt electric architecture and is capable of charging from 20 to 80 percent in a claimed 28 minutes on a DC fast charger. Level 2 charging on a 240-volt circuit should take the battery from 5 to 80 percent in roughly 7 hours. Drivers with no other option other than plugging into a typical 110-volt household circuit best pack a book or three, as the estimated time for a 5-80 percent charge in that scenario is up to 52 hours.

The EPA hasn’t released fuel economy for the Overland yet, but the Moab is rated for 80 MPGe city, 62 MPGe highway, and 71 MPGe combined. Second Row: It's a pretty standard affair in the back, with 60/40 split bench seating in the second row. Heated outboard second-row seats are available as part of the optional Comfort Package.

Cargo Capacity: In addition to the 30 cubic feet of cargo space behind the Recon’s rear seats, it also features a small 3.0-cubic-foot frunk under the hood—a perk of being an EV.

The Recon's interior features a central 14.5-inch infotainment display and a 12.3-inch digital gauge display offering readouts for the driver.

The company's Uconnect 5 software interface allows users to access all sorts of features, including Apple CarPlay, Android Auto, SiriusXM satellite radio, integrated navigation, Amazon FireTV and Alexa, and a 4G LTE Wi-Fi hotspot.

The Recon comes standard with many safety and assistance features, including adaptive cruise control, lane-keeping assistance, a 360-degree surround camera, and parking assist.

#4502. GTA 6 Gets Massive New Screenshot Gallery Two Weeks Before Launch

After years of waiting, we're finally just two weeks away from Grand Theft Auto 6, and Rockstar Games apparently isn't done giving us things to obsess over before launch. The developer has just released 38 new screenshots, offering another look at Vice City and the surrounding state of Leonida before we finally get to explore it ourselves on November 19.

There's quite a bit to unpack here, too. The images cover everything from Jason and Lucia to the city's nightlife, criminal underworld, and quieter corners of Leonida. But what really caught our attention was the character detail. The facial details are astonishingly realistic, and we're not just talking about Jason and Lucia. A few of the background characters look good enough to have their own stories.

Take-Two may go nuclear as GTA 6 release draws near.

Of course, there's plenty more to admire beyond the characters themselves. The screenshots also give us a closer look at the people, places, and everyday scenes that could make Leonida feel like an actual place.

Rockstar unveiled the new collection on November 5 through its official GTA 6 launch gallery, inviting us to take another look around Leonida before release day.

While the screenshots include the usual assortment of cars, guns, and criminal activities, some of the most impressive images are simply close-ups of the characters themselves.

Lucia, for instance, appears in several tense situations, including one screenshot where she's aiming a handgun directly ahead. The detail in her face is striking, from the texture of her skin and individual strands of hair to the subtle expressions that make her look far more believable than the characters we've grown accustomed to seeing in open-world games.

Jason gets similar treatment, whether he's working out shirtless, confronting armed enemies, or finding himself in the middle of another chaotic encounter. Even the supporting characters and seemingly ordinary NPCs look remarkably detailed.

One particularly impressive close-up shows a man partially covering his face with his hand, with the lighting bringing out the finer details of his eyes, skin, and jewelry. Other screenshots feature heavily tattooed individuals, some sporting elaborate hairstyles and accessories, whose appearances are distinctive enough to suggest considerable attention has gone into the wider population.

That's particularly encouraging for a game like GTA 6, where so much of the fun comes from simply wandering around, getting distracted, and observing whatever nonsense the locals are getting up to.

A few of the background characters look good enough to have their own stories.

The nightlife screenshots are especially interesting in this regard. One shows a stripper performing under the neon lights of a cabaret, while another features several women gathered inside what appears to be a strip club dressing room. Elsewhere, packed dance floors, colorful lighting, and partygoers enjoying themselves offer another glimpse of Vice City's entertainment scene.

There are also several images featuring tattooed street crews and other figures who wouldn't look out of place in Leonida's criminal underworld. One shows a group of men posing together, while another features a man standing beside a muscular dog adorned with a gold chain.

There's even a gathering around heavily customized tuners, which makes us wonder just how much further Rockstar has taken GTA's car culture this time around. Between the customization and the street meets, there's certainly room for something more elaborate than what we had in GTA 5.

Taken together, these images give us a better sense of the people and communities we might encounter throughout Leonida, rather than focusing exclusively on Jason and Lucia's criminal exploits.

Of course, the latest collection isn't entirely concerned with its inhabitants. Rockstar has included several environmental shots that offer another look at the scale and variety of GTA 6's open world.

Vice City's waterfront appears particularly impressive, with boats gathered around a marina and high-rise buildings dominating the skyline. Another image captures the city after dark, with illuminated skyscrapers stretching into the distance.

There are quieter scenes, too. One screenshot shows an almost deserted landscape at sunset, with a solitary tree overlooking the distant city skyline. Others take us into the Grassrivers, where alligators and airboats feature prominently. An underwater shot at Leonida Keys also shows a coral reef teeming with marine life, making us wonder whether scuba diving will actually feel more rewarding this time around, especially if there's more to discover beneath the surface.

These contrasts have been an important part of GTA 6's marketing. Vice City might be the main attraction, but Rockstar has repeatedly emphasized that Leonida extends well beyond its urban areas, encompassing everything from tropical islands to swamps and rural communities.

Rockstar's previous open-world games have been praised for their environmental detail and the behavior of their NPCs, particularly Red Dead Redemption 2. Whether GTA 6 can achieve something similar on a much larger, more densely populated scale remains to be seen, but these images certainly make a promising first impression.

Naturally, screenshots alone can't tell us how these environments and characters will behave during actual gameplay. Nevertheless, the sheer amount of visual detail on display makes it difficult not to get excited about finally exploring Leonida.

Fortunately, that wait is almost over. GTA 6 launches on November 19, 2026, for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, with pre-loading beginning November 10.

After all these years, it's strange to think we're finally this close to getting our hands on GTA 6.

According to a new rumor, Rockstar Games could release the GTA 6 PC port just a few months after the highly anticipated console launch.

#4501. Toyota Quietly Gave The 2027 Toyota RAV4 PHEV A Big Upgrade

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Toyota has quietly upgraded the sixth-generation RAV4 Plug-in Hybrid. All trims of the model year 2027 RAV4 PHEV now get a Tesla-style North American Charging Standard (NACS) port straight from the factory—plus fast-charging capability.

That’s a pretty big deal for a few key reasons. When the RAV4 PHEV launched last year, it arrived with a CCS charging port at a time when all new EVs had started transitioning to native NACS ports. At the time, only the PHEV XSE and Woodland trims could fast charge, meaning you had to pay at least a $4,000 premium for the capability.

Now that fast-charging capability expands to the full PHEV lineup, all the way down to the entry SE model, which costs $42,100. The same goes for the top-trim GR Sport. Owners can now simply drive the 2027 RAV4 PHEV to Tesla Superchargers or any of the new stations equipped with NACS cables. It will charge at maximum rate of 50 kilowatts, enough to go from 10-80% in just 30 minutes.

Moreover, not many PHEVs get fast-charging capability, let alone native NACS ports. The RAV4 PHEV is now the first and only major PHEV in the U.S. to transition to the NACS port, joining the wave of new fully electric models doing the same.

Some other notable PHEVs that have fast-charging capability include the Mercedes GLC 350e which gets a CCS port and the Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV which gets the outdated CHAdeMO connector.

If owners are used to plugging-in at home, they can continue to do so. The RAV4 PHEV gets an onboard AC charger for Level 1 and Level 2 charging. And home charging can now be faster as well, with GR Sport and SE trims getting 11 kW AC charging, up from 7 kW before. The XSE and Woodland were already rated for 11 kW since last year.

And the one final notable upgrade is that the charging port is now located near the driver’s side door—it was previously at the passenger’s side. This could be useful depending on how you park at home and where you live, since there’s no industry standard for the charging port location.

The newer V4 Tesla Superchargers, as well as Ionna, Walmart, and pretty much every major new station have long cables with well-engineered retraction systems, so the location of the port shouldn’t be a problem. The older V3 Tesla Superchargers will be a challenge since they were designed for rear left ports.

The RAV4 PHEV gets up to 52 miles of EPA range from its 22.7 kilowatt-hour lithium-ion battery. If you regularly plug it in, you can cover your everyday driving needs using battery power alone and use the gas engine for longer trips. And now, it looks like that charging experience just got a little better.

#4500. How a metabolite protects the enzyme that consumes it

Metabolites are consumed by enzymes to produce other vital molecules as well as to control metabolite levels. But how do cells avoid consuming too much? Researchers from the MPI of Biochemistry, with the University of Nevada, Las Vegas, and the de Duve Institute in Brussels, have deciphered such molecular regulation in tryptophan metabolism. The essential amino acid tryptophan binds to a second site on the enzyme TDO2, distinct from where it is consumed. This sequesters a region needed by two effectors, the kinase CK2 and the ubiquitin ligase CUL1–β-TrCP, which act sequentially to signal TDO2 degradation. The findings are now published in Molecular Cell.

#4499. Amazon set to deploy more than 3,000 TATA electric delivery trucks

Amazon isn’t just electrifying its American delivery operations. The virtual big box stores that Bezos built understands the benefits of EVs as well as anyone, and they’re working hard to deploy electric vehicles everywhere they can. And now, that global push is extending to India.

Indian automaker TATA Motors has announced a deal with Amazon to deploy 3,000 electric trucks across Amazon’s transportation network in India. When it goes live, it will be the largest electric truck deployment by in India and mark Amazon’s most significant move to extend its Indian fleet electrification beyond last-mile logistics.

“India is accelerating towards electric mobility and the realization of Viksit Bharat 2047,” says Shri H.D. Kumaraswamy, Hon’ble Union Minister for Heavy Industries and Steel, Government of India. “The collaboration between TATA Motors and Amazon shows what that looks like in practice: sustained demand from a nationwide logistics network met by electric trucks manufactured in India. Through PM E-DRIVE, the Government will continue to support this transition, and I look forward to more such efforts in powering green logistics.”

In addition to being a big deal for TATA, the 3,000 electric truck deal represents a serous bump to India’s deployed electric truck fleet, and are a major step towards the wide-scale electrification of freight transportation across the country – that’s not just good for Amazon’s fuel bills, it’s good for everyone and everything that breathes air, too.

“Electrifying our logistics and transportation network is an important part of Amazon’s goal to achieve net-zero carbon emissions by 2040,” says Abhinav Singh, Vice President, Operations, Amazon, APAC, Middle East, Africa and Turkey. “We have made significant progress in India, with more than 15,000 electric vehicles operating across 500-plus cities. To enable this transition, we are also supporting the development of infrastructure and solutions that make EV adoption easier for our carrier partners and drivers. We are now setting a bold vision to scale electric trucking, addressing one of the toughest challenges in decarbonizing transportation. Our collaboration with TATA Motors marks an important step towards realizing this vision. By combining our strengths, we aim to accelerate the deployment of electric trucks across more routes, starting with intracity operations and expanding to India’s major freight corridors.”

The truck Amazon will be deploying in these record numbers is a version of the Tata Ultra E.7, a 7.5-tonne (~16,000 lb.) straight truck powered by a 240 kW (~320 hp) electric motor drawing power from a 96 kWh LFP battery pack. The truck’s makers claim a loaded range of up to 130 km (~80 miles) on a single charge, with DC fast-charging that’s capable enough to keep the trucks charged up between deliveries.

Amazon’s new TATA electric delivery trucks will support the transport of goods between warehouse facilities – which means traveling across cities and along India’s national freight corridors.

Typically, when "$300,000" and "pony" appear in the same sentence, what's likely the subject of discussion is purebred racehorses. The talk, however, could now also be about the Ford Mustang GTD. If its name, ultrawide bodywork, carbon-fiber diffusers, and shade-casting rear wing weren’t dead giveaways, know that the GTD is as close as you can get to an IMSA race car for the road. In fact, with 815 horsepower supplied by a supercharged 5.2-liter V-8, it has far more power than the Mustang GT3 race cars that competed in this year's 24 Hours of Le Mans.

Power is only one aspect of the GTD's expansive performance envelope, and with a carbon fiber body, sophisticated underbody active aerodynamics, and a race-car-derived inboard pushrod suspension setup where a standard 'Stang's rear seats would be, it's no wonder why Ford's ultimate pony is the second fastest production car around the Nürburgring Nordschleife. As is usually the case, performance comes at a cost. In the GTD's case, that is both literal and figurative, with its supercar-rivaling MSRP and a dearth of space for either passengers or cargo.

Expert Tip: With 1250 horsepower, a 0-60-mph sprint time of 2.1 seconds, and a starting price $100,000 less than the GTD, the Corvette ZR1X arguably offers a superior performance-to-price ratio than Ford's ultimate Mustang.

Compare the 2027 Ford Mustang GTD with the top vehicles in this segment with our new compare tool.

We expect that the Ford Mustang GTD will gallop into the 2027 model year without any notable changes.

If this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying new.

With 815 horsepower from its supercharged 5.2-liter V-8 engine, the road-going car has far more power than the Mustang GT3 race car it shares styling with. That track-only model instead uses a 5.4-liter V-8 with around 550 horsepower. Cog swaps for the GTD come courtesy of a rear-mounted eight-speed dual-clutch automated transaxle, similar to the type of gearbox used in the race car.

A Mustang GTD we tested blew us away with its performance. Its shockingly civilized on-road ride quality surprised us as well. We would welcome more steering feedback, but the supremely balanced handling and staggering levels of grip make for a world-class driving experience.

In Comparison: The Mustang GTD is quick, but two other rear-drive rockets, the Chevrolet Corvette ZR1 and Porsche 911 GT3 RS, outran it to 60 mph in our testing, completing that task in 2.2 and 2.7 seconds, respectively.

The Ford Mustang GTD prioritizes lap times over fuel economy, as the roar from its mighty supercharged V-8 quickly reveals. As a result, the GTD only manages a pitiful 10 mpg in the city, 17 mpg on the highway, and 12 mpg combined, according to the EPA. For more information about the Mustang GTD's fuel economy, visit the EPA's website.

First Row: Though it looks every bit like the Mustang GT3 purpose-built race car on the outside, the GTD's cabin looks a lot like any ol' Mustang's. Suede, leather, and carbon fiber are the main ingredients of the GTD's interior that upgrade it from its lesser kin—though not by much. Recaro bucket seats hug both driver and front passenger, but the GTD jettisons the rear seats of other Mustang models. The paddle shifters are 3D-printed from titanium, same for the rotary dial gear selector and serial placard. Ford claims it sourced the material for these components from retired Lockheed Martin F-22 fighter jets.

Cargo Capacity: The trunk is a treasure box of suspension and cooling components, so forget bringing luggage to track-day events.

The Mustang GTD packs a 12.4-inch digital gauge cluster and a 13.2-inch touchscreen infotainment display. Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are standard equipment. Though the system is largely the same as that of other Mustangs, it does include additional GTD-exclusive performance menus.

As you'd expect of a car like this, the GTD doesn't have many driver-assistance features, but it does have a lane-keep assist system and automatic emergency braking.

For information about the GTD's crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites.

The Mustang GTD has a solid but average warranty. However, unlike rival Chevy, Ford doesn't provide a complimentary scheduled maintenance visit.

#4497. Air holes turn silicon wafers into flat ultraviolet focusing mirrors for compact optics

Traditional lenses and mirrors focus light using curved surfaces. Metasurfaces can achieve similar functions with a flat layer of nanoscale structures that locally control the phase of light. #4494. Gray Zone Warfare Update Addresses Biggest Rogue Ops Concerns

Lauren has experience in the gaming and esports space, writing news, guides, features, reviews, lists, conducting interviews, and more. Before joining the team at DualShockers, Lauren was a Features Writer at Adventure Gamers, a Guides Writer at Gameranx, as well as contributing as a News Writer at PCInvasion and Daily

Gray Zone Warfare stands out for its immersion as a PvE open-world tactical shooter set on a quarantined Southeast Asian island with plenty of narrative elements to get stuck into. Rogue Ops allows for a fresh experience by building your very own Hideout and growing your reputation in new ways.

The ambitious mode has a lot to love, but it has faced its fair share of player complaints, as major issues have been interrupting the fun in the gameplay loop. A Halloween Dev Stream teased significant improvements to enemy AI and making the Hideout economy more rewarding.

This is the detailed all purpose hub for Gray Zone Warfare guides and content.

Now that Gray Zone Warfare Patch 0.5.1.0 is live, we can dive into all the key changes you can expect to see when you embark on your next mission.

First of all, huge changes have been made to the way enemy AI behaves. One of the biggest criticisms players had of the AI enemies was their inconsistency and the feeling of them being extremely overpowered.

Following this update, enemies should no longer know your exact position after shooting. Sound now only gives them an approximate location, meaning the farther away you are, the more difficult it is for them to detect you. Rather than the AI instantly sharing your exact position, they'll rely on information they can gather, which ultimately makes their reactions more natural.

Stealth has also undergone some work to make it more consistent. Moving slowly should make you harder to detect, and the AI exhibits reactions to light that you’d expect. These changes should make stealth, flanking enemies, and repositioning more rewarding and allow you to take a greater advantage over your surroundings.

Improvements have also been made to how enemies engage in combat. Trained soldiers bring more precision to their combat abilities and make better use of cover, but untrained enemies will be more careless in their actions.

Combined with fixing pesky problems with hit boxes, grenades, and enemies getting stuck behind doors, this series of changes aims to make combat more varied and test your tactical performance.

Sound now only gives them an approximate location, meaning the farther away you are, the more difficult it is for them to detect you.

Another major change has been made to the economy in Hideout. A range of rewards have been increased, including raising the rewards from smuggling tasks and increasing the sales prices of smuggling backpacks, and improving rewards from hideout handovers and increasing the sale prices of hideout products.

Production and disassembly times have even been reduced across the board, and the size and weight of selected building materials and disassembly have been reduced for a better looting experience.

The Gray Zone Warfare update arrives with a slew of bug fixes to gameplay, animations, audio, tasks, and so much more. This includes fixing a bug where the health panel could show 100% damage on an organ that was not destroyed and repairing an issue that caused some tasks to not be offered due to a nearby task blocking them. The full patch notes can be viewed here.

In the meantime, the team will continue to address further feedback, like AI enemies seemingly taking too many shots to kill, provided as an example, with further fixes planned for upcoming patches. The developers are already working on their next major update, Patch 0.5.2.0.
